vocab.ex: Babies cannot digest some foods that adults eat.
vocab.exzh: 嬰兒無法消化一些大人吃的食物。

vocab.ex: The smell of fried chicken filled my mouth with saliva.
vocab.exzh: 炸雞的香味讓我口水直流。

vocab.ex: Chew your food well before you swallow it.
vocab.exzh: 食物要嚼爛再吞下去。

vocab.ex: My stomach is growling, so it must be lunchtime.
vocab.exzh: 我的肚子在咕嚕咕嚕叫，一定是午餐時間到了。

vocab.ex: Lemon juice contains a mild acid.
vocab.exzh: 檸檬汁含有溫和的酸。

vocab.ex: The small intestine is longer than the large one.
vocab.exzh: 小腸比大腸還長。

vocab.ex: Plants take nutrients from the soil.
vocab.exzh: 植物從土壤吸取養分。

vocab.ex: A sponge absorbs water.
vocab.exzh: 海綿會吸水。

kinds_head.eyebrow: Helpers Along the Way · 沿路的幫手
kinds_head.en: Food never passes through these, but they make digestion work
kinds_head.zh: 食物不經過它們，消化卻少不了它們

kinds.control_en: About 1 liter of saliva a day
kinds.text_en: Chewing makes the pieces small, so the juices that come later can reach more of the food.
kinds.text_zh: 咀嚼把食物弄小，後面的消化液才能接觸到更多食物。

kinds.text_en: Makes bile, which breaks fat into tiny drops, and also checks and cleans the blood coming from the intestines.
kinds.text_zh: 製造膽汁，把油脂分散成小油滴；也檢查、淨化從腸子送來的血液。

kinds.text_en: A small green bag that squeezes bile into the small intestine when a fatty meal arrives.
kinds.text_zh: 一個綠色的小袋子；油膩的食物一到，就把膽汁擠進小腸。

kinds.text_en: Its juices break down starch, protein, and fat. It also makes insulin, which controls the sugar in your blood.
kinds.text_zh: 它的消化液能分解澱粉、蛋白質和脂肪；它也製造胰島素，控制血液裡的糖。

kinds.text_en: Helpful bacteria break down fiber, make some vitamins, and help keep harmful germs out.
kinds.text_zh: 好細菌分解纖維、製造一些維生素，還幫忙擋住壞病菌。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Digestion is a team job: the tube moves the food, and the helpers add the juices that break it apart.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 消化是團隊合作：管子負責搬運食物，幫手負責加入分解它的消化液。

measure.title_en: Taste your saliva at work, and find your lunch
measure.title_zh: 嚐嚐唾液在工作，再找找你的午餐
measure.lead_en: Two quick experiments you can do with your own body, and one you can do with the model.
measure.lead_zh: 兩個用自己身體就能做的小實驗，再加一個和模型一起做的。

steps.en: The cracker test
steps.zh: 蘇打餅乾試驗
steps.text_en: Chew a plain, unsalted cracker for 60 seconds without swallowing. Does it start to taste a little sweet? That is saliva turning starch into sugar.
steps.text_zh: 把一片原味、不加鹽的蘇打餅乾嚼 60 秒，先不要吞。有沒有開始覺得有點甜？那就是唾液把澱粉變成糖。

steps.en: Count your chews
steps.zh: 數一數咀嚼次數
steps.text_en: At lunch, count how many times you chew one bite before you swallow. Try to reach 20.
steps.text_zh: 吃午餐時，數數看一口飯嚼幾下才吞下去，試著嚼到 20 下。

steps.en: Where is my lunch now?
steps.zh: 我的午餐現在在哪？
steps.text_en: Type the time you ate lunch into the model and press the button. It uses the real time right now.
steps.text_zh: 在模型裡輸入你吃午餐的時間，按下按鈕。它會用現在的真實時間計算。

myths.myth_en: Swallowed gum stays in your stomach for seven years.
myths.myth_zh: 吞下去的口香糖會在胃裡待七年。
myths.fact_en: Your body cannot digest gum, but it does not stay. It moves through and leaves the body within a few days, like other things you cannot digest. Still, gum is for chewing, not swallowing.
myths.fact_zh: 身體無法消化口香糖，但它不會留下來；它會和其他無法消化的東西一樣，幾天內就排出體外。不過口香糖還是用來嚼的，不是用來吞的。

myths.myth_en: Most digestion happens in the stomach.
myths.myth_zh: 消化大部分在胃裡完成。
myths.fact_en: The stomach churns and starts breaking food down, but most digestion, and almost all the taking in of nutrients, happens in the small intestine.
myths.fact_zh: 胃負責攪拌、開始分解，但大部分的消化，以及幾乎全部的養分吸收，都在小腸裡進行。

myths.myth_en: Food falls down to your stomach because of gravity.
myths.myth_zh: 食物是靠重力掉進胃裡的。
myths.fact_en: Muscles in the esophagus squeeze the food along. That is why you can swallow lying down, and why astronauts can eat in space.
myths.fact_zh: 是食道的肌肉把食物擠下去的。所以躺著也能吞，太空人在太空中也能吃東西。

myths.myth_en: Stomach ulcers are mostly caused by stress and spicy food.
myths.myth_zh: 胃潰瘍主要是壓力和吃辣造成的。
myths.fact_en: Many ulcers are caused by a kind of bacteria called H. pylori. Two Australian doctors showed this, and one of them even drank the bacteria to prove it. They won a Nobel Prize in 2005.
myths.fact_zh: 許多胃潰瘍其實是一種叫幽門螺旋桿菌的細菌造成的。兩位澳洲醫生證明了這件事，其中一位甚至親自喝下細菌來證明，兩人在 2005 年獲得諾貝爾獎。

tricks.title_en: Chew, churn, soak up, dry out
tricks.body_en: Mouth chews, stomach churns, small intestine soaks up nutrients, large intestine takes back water.
tricks.body_zh: 嘴巴咀嚼、胃攪拌、小腸吸收養分、大腸把水收回來。

tricks.title_en: Small is long, large is wide
tricks.body_en: The names are about width, not length: the small intestine is about 5 meters long, the large intestine only about 1.5 meters, but much wider.
tricks.body_zh: 名字說的是粗細，不是長短：小腸約 5 公尺長，大腸只有約 1.5 公尺，卻粗得多。

tricks.body_en: Food is squeezed through your whole digestive tract by waves of muscle, from your throat to the very end.
tricks.body_zh: 從喉嚨到最後，食物一路都是被一波波的肌肉擠著走，不是自己掉下去的。

tricks.title_en: From lunch to the end: one to three days
tricks.title_zh: 從午餐到最後：一到三天
tricks.body_en: Minutes in the mouth, seconds down the esophagus, hours in the stomach and small intestine, a day or more in the large intestine.
tricks.body_zh: 嘴裡幾分鐘、食道幾秒、胃和小腸幾個小時、大腸一天以上。

materials.en: A ball of yarn or string, at least 8 meters
materials.zh: 一捲毛線或棉線，至少 8 公尺

materials.en: A meter stick or tape measure
materials.zh: 一支公尺尺或捲尺

materials.en: Labels or sticky notes
materials.zh: 標籤或便利貼

steps.en: Measure and cut four pieces: esophagus 25 cm, stomach 25 cm, small intestine 5 m, large intestine 1.5 m.
steps.zh: 量好、剪下四段：食道 25 公分、胃 25 公分、小腸 5 公尺、大腸 1.5 公尺。

steps.en: Tie them together in order and label each part.
steps.zh: 依順序綁在一起，每一段貼上名稱。

steps.en: Stretch the whole thing down the hallway. Which part is longest by far?
steps.zh: 把整條拉直放在走廊上。哪一段長得最多？

steps.en: Discuss: how does all of that fit inside your belly?
steps.zh: 討論：這麼長的東西，怎麼裝得進肚子裡？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: these are rough adult lengths, and in a living person the small intestine is often shorter because its muscles keep it bunched up. Coil the small-intestine string into a small pile to show how it fits.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：這些是成人的大約長度；在活人身上，小腸常常比較短，因為肌肉讓它保持收縮。把代表小腸的那段線盤成一小堆，就看得出它怎麼塞進肚子。

activities.title_en: A Stomach in a Zipper Bag

materials.en: A strong zipper bag (the stomach)
materials.zh: 一個堅固的夾鏈袋（胃）

materials.en: Two plain crackers and a small piece of banana
materials.zh: 兩片原味餅乾和一小塊香蕉

materials.en: Half a cup of water with a little lemon juice (the stomach juices)
materials.zh: 半杯加了一點檸檬汁的水（胃液）

materials.en: An old stocking or tights, a bowl, and scissors
materials.zh: 一隻舊絲襪或褲襪、一個碗、一把剪刀

steps.en: Break the crackers and banana into the bag, add the lemon water, and seal it tight.
steps.zh: 把餅乾和香蕉剝碎放進袋子，倒入檸檬水，把袋口封緊。

steps.en: Squeeze and knead the bag for two minutes. This is the stomach churning.
steps.zh: 揉捏袋子兩分鐘——這就是胃在攪拌。

steps.en: Cut off one corner and squeeze the mush into the stocking over the bowl. This is the small intestine.
steps.zh: 剪開一個角，在碗上方把糊糊擠進絲襪裡——這就是小腸。

steps.en: Squeeze the stocking gently from top to bottom. What drips into the bowl, and what stays inside?
steps.zh: 從上往下輕輕擠絲襪。滴進碗裡的是什麼？留在裡面的又是什麼？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the liquid that drips through stands for the nutrients passing into the blood, and what stays inside moves on to the large intestine. Do not eat the materials, and wipe up spills right away.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：滴下來的液體代表進入血液的養分，留在絲襪裡的就是接下來要進大腸的部分。材料不可以吃，打翻了要馬上擦乾淨。

culture.title_en: Dissolve and Transform, and a Date Swallowed Whole
culture.body_en: The Chinese word for digestion, 消化 (xiāohuà), joins 消, to melt away, with 化, to change. Chinese also uses it for ideas: to 消化 a lesson means to really understand it. The idiom 囫圇吞棗 describes swallowing a date whole without chewing, which means reading or learning something without taking it in. The opposite advice for eating is 細嚼慢嚥: chew finely, swallow slowly. And the everyday word for a meal, 吃飯, simply means to eat rice.
culture.body_zh: 中文的「消化」由「消」（消融）和「化」（變化）組成。中文也拿它來說學習：把一課「消化」了，就是真的懂了。成語「囫圇吞棗」是說整顆棗子沒嚼就吞下去，比喻讀書學習不求理解。吃東西的相反建議是「細嚼慢嚥」。而日常說的「吃飯」，字面上就是吃米飯。

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If you have a very bad stomachache, keep throwing up, or see blood, tell an adult right away. Before tasting anything in class, check for food allergies, and wash your hands.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果肚子非常痛、一直吐，或看到血，請馬上告訴大人。課堂上試吃任何東西之前，先確認有沒有食物過敏，也要洗手。

lessons.title: How Does Your Brain Talk to Your Body?
lessons.blurb_en: Signals race along your nerves faster than a bullet train. Watch them in slow motion, find out why a reflex beats thinking, and test your own reaction time.
lessons.blurb_zh: 訊號沿著神經奔馳，比高鐵還快。用慢動作看它們傳遞，弄懂為什麼反射比思考快，再測測自己的反應時間。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your nerves carry signals in two directions: from your senses to your brain, and from your brain to your muscles. For some emergencies, your spinal cord takes a shortcut and acts before your brain even knows.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 神經把訊號往兩個方向送：從感官送到大腦，再從大腦送到肌肉。遇到某些緊急狀況，脊髓會走捷徑，在大腦知道之前就先行動。

lab.how_en: Pick a moment, and glowing signals travel along the nerves in slow motion while the clock counts real milliseconds. Compare catching a ruler, which needs your brain, with touching a hot pan, where your spinal cord acts first. Then take the reaction test below the model, and play the ruler catch at your own speed.
lab.how_zh: 選一個情境，發亮的訊號會用慢動作沿著神經傳遞，時鐘顯示真實的毫秒數。比一比「接住尺」（需要大腦）和「碰到燙鍋子」（脊髓先行動）。再做模型下方的反應測驗，用你自己的速度播放「接住尺」。

legend.en: Glowing dots: nerve signals
legend.zh: 發亮的點：神經訊號

legend.en: Orange dot: the slower pain signal
legend.zh: 橘色的點：比較慢的痛覺訊號

legend.en: Yellow lines: the spinal cord and nerves
legend.zh: 黃色的線：脊髓與神經

legend.en: Colored areas: parts of the brain at work (vision, thinking, movement, touch)
legend.zh: 上色的區域：正在工作的大腦區域（視覺、思考、運動、觸覺）

The milliseconds are typical estimates: nerve signals travel at roughly 50 to 120 meters per second, muscles take tens of milliseconds to tighten, and pain from heat travels on much slower nerves.
lab.scale_zh: 骨頭是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架；大腦和神經是簡化的示意圖，真實的神經會分出成千上萬條小分支。毫秒數是一般的估計：神經訊號每秒大約跑 50 到 120 公尺，肌肉收緊要幾十毫秒，被燙到的痛覺則走在慢得多的神經上。

steps.en: The ruler starts to fall. Your eyes see it move.
steps.zh: 尺開始往下掉，眼睛看到它在動。

steps.en: The vision area at the back of your brain makes sense of it.
steps.zh: 後腦的視覺區看懂了。

steps.en: The front of your brain decides: catch it!
steps.zh: 前額的大腦做出決定：接住它！

steps.en: The movement area of the left brain sends the order. The left brain runs the right hand.
steps.zh: 左腦的運動區送出命令：左腦管右手。

steps.en: The order crosses over, races down the spinal cord, and out to the arm.
steps.zh: 命令交叉到另一邊，沿著脊髓往下衝，再傳到手臂。

steps.en: Hand muscles squeeze. Caught! About 0.2 seconds in all.
steps.zh: 手部肌肉收緊，接住了！全部大約 0.2 秒。

ruler.note_en: Most of the time goes into seeing and deciding, not into the trip along the nerves.
ruler.note_zh: 大部分的時間花在看和決定，而不是訊號沿著神經跑。

steps.en: Your fingertips touch the hot pan.
steps.zh: 指尖碰到燙鍋子。

steps.en: A fast signal reaches the spinal cord.
steps.zh: 快速的訊號抵達脊髓。

steps.en: The spinal cord sends “pull away!” straight back to the arm. No brain needed.
steps.zh: 脊髓直接回送「縮回來！」給手臂，不需要大腦。

steps.en: A copy of the signal reaches your brain, which notices the touch.
steps.zh: 訊號的副本也送到大腦，大腦注意到被碰了一下。

steps.en: Your hand jerks back.
steps.zh: 手猛然縮回來。

steps.en: The burning pain arrives last, on slower nerves. Ouch!
steps.zh: 灼熱的痛覺走比較慢的神經，最後才到：好燙！

hot.note_en: This is a reflex: your hand is already safe before you feel the pain.
hot.note_zh: 這就是反射：你還沒感覺到痛，手就已經脫離危險了。

steps.en: A doctor taps the tendon just below the kneecap.
steps.zh: 醫生輕敲髕骨下方的肌腱。

steps.en: The signal runs up the thigh to the spinal cord in the lower back.
steps.zh: 訊號沿著大腿跑到下背部的脊髓。

steps.en: The spinal cord answers right away: tighten the thigh muscle.
steps.zh: 脊髓馬上回答：收緊大腿肌肉。

steps.en: The lower leg kicks out, all by itself.
steps.zh: 小腿自己踢了出去。

knee.note_en: Doctors use this test to check that the nerves and spinal cord are working.
knee.note_zh: 醫生用這個測試檢查神經和脊髓是否正常。

steps.en: You decide to wiggle your toes. The movement area of the brain fires.
steps.zh: 你決定動動腳趾，大腦的運動區發出訊號。

steps.en: The order runs down the whole spinal cord.
steps.zh: 命令沿著整條脊髓往下跑。

steps.en: It leaves the backbone and travels down the leg.
steps.zh: 它離開脊柱，沿著腿往下走。

steps.en: Toe muscles tighten. Your toes wiggle.
steps.zh: 腳趾的肌肉收緊，腳趾動了。

toes.note_en: This is the longest trip in your body, well over a meter, yet it still takes only a few hundredths of a second.
toes.note_zh: 這是身體裡最長的一段路，超過一公尺，卻也只要百分之幾秒。

paras: Someone tosses you a ball. In less than half a second, your eyes see it, your brain figures out where it is going, and your arms move to catch it. All of that is the work of your nervous system: your brain, your spinal cord, and the nerves that reach every part of your body. An adult brain weighs only about 1.4 kilograms, but it has around 86 billion nerve cells, and it uses about a fifth of all the energy your body burns.

Nerve cells, called neurons, are long and thin, and they pass messages as tiny electrical signals. The fastest signals travel at about 120 meters per second, more than 400 kilometers an hour, which is faster than Taiwan's high-speed rail. Nerves are bundles of these cells, and they carry messages in two directions. Sensory nerves bring news in from your eyes, ears, skin, and other senses. Motor nerves carry orders out to your muscles.

Your spinal cord is the main cable. It is about as thick as your finger and about 45 centimeters long, protected inside your backbone, and pairs of nerves branch off it to every part of the body. At the top sits the brain. The large, wrinkly cerebrum handles thinking, the senses, and movement. Its two halves cross over: the left half runs the right side of your body, and the right half runs the left. The cerebellum at the back helps with balance and smooth movement, and the brainstem keeps you breathing and keeps your heart beating without you ever thinking about it.

Some messages never wait for the brain. If you touch a hot pan, a signal shoots to your spinal cord, and the spinal cord sends an order straight back: pull away! Your hand moves before you even feel the pain, which arrives a moment later on slower nerves. This kind of automatic, lightning-fast action is called a reflex. When a doctor taps just below your knee and your leg kicks, that is a reflex too, and it shows the doctor that your nerves are working.

Things that need a decision take longer. To catch a falling ruler, your eyes must see it, your brain must decide, and then the order must travel down to your hand. For most people, that takes about two tenths of a second, and during that time the ruler falls about 20 centimeters. Practice can make you a little faster. Being tired or distracted, for example by looking at a phone, makes you slower, which is why it is dangerous to cross the street while texting.

Your brain changes every time you learn something. Each time you practice a skill, the connections between your neurons get stronger, which is why practice makes things easier. Sleep matters too: while you sleep, your brain sorts and stores what you learned during the day. And because your brain cannot be replaced, wear a helmet when you ride a bike or scooter. Now try the reaction test below the model and see how far your ruler falls.
paras_zh: 有人丟給你一顆球。不到半秒，你的眼睛看到它、大腦算出它要往哪裡飛、手臂就動起來接住它。這一切都是神經系統的工作：大腦、脊髓，以及通到身體每個角落的神經。成人的大腦只有大約 1.4 公斤，卻有大約 860 億個神經細胞，而且用掉全身大約五分之一的能量。
神經細胞又叫神經元，又長又細，靠微小的電訊號傳遞訊息。最快的訊號每秒大約跑 120 公尺，也就是時速四百多公里，比台灣高鐵還快。神經是一束束的神經細胞，往兩個方向傳遞訊息：感覺神經把眼睛、耳朵、皮膚等感官的消息送進來，運動神經把命令送出去給肌肉。
脊髓是主幹線。它大約和手指一樣粗、大約 45 公分長，受到脊柱的保護，一對對的神經從它分出去，通到身體各處。最上面是大腦。又大又皺的大腦負責思考、感覺和動作，它的左右兩半是交叉的：左半邊管身體右側，右半邊管身體左側。後面的小腦幫忙維持平衡、讓動作順暢；腦幹則讓你持續呼吸、心臟持續跳動，完全不需要你去想。
有些訊息根本不等大腦。如果你碰到燙鍋子，訊號會衝到脊髓，脊髓直接回送命令：縮回來！你的手在感覺到痛之前就已經移開了，痛覺要再過一下子，才沿著比較慢的神經抵達。這種自動、閃電般的動作叫做反射。醫生輕敲你膝蓋下方、你的腿自己踢出去，也是一種反射，這讓醫生知道你的神經運作正常。
需要做決定的事就比較慢。要接住一把掉下來的尺，眼睛得先看到、大腦得做決定，命令再一路傳到手。大多數人大約要零點二秒，這段時間裡尺大約掉了 20 公分。練習能讓你快一點；累了或分心（例如看手機）就會變慢，所以邊走路邊滑手機過馬路很危險。
你每學一樣新東西，大腦就會改變一點。每練習一次，神經元之間的連結就更強，所以越練越容易。睡眠也很重要：睡覺時，大腦會整理、儲存你白天學到的東西。而且大腦無法替換，所以騎腳踏車或滑板車時要戴安全帽。現在試試看模型下方的反應測驗，看看你的尺會掉多遠。
questions: What is the difference between sensory nerves and motor nerves?
Why does your hand pull away from a hot pan before you feel the pain?
Why is it dangerous to cross the street while texting?
answers: Sensory nerves carry messages from the senses in to the spinal cord and brain. Motor nerves carry orders out to the muscles.
It is a reflex: the signal goes to the spinal cord, which sends an order straight back to the arm without waiting for the brain. The pain arrives later on slower nerves.
Being distracted slows your reaction time, so it takes longer to see a car, decide, and move out of the way.

vocab.ex: Your brain keeps working even while you sleep.
vocab.exzh: 就算你在睡覺，大腦也一直在工作。

vocab.ex: The dentist made the nerve in my tooth numb before fixing it.
vocab.exzh: 牙醫先讓我牙齒的神經麻掉，才開始治療。

vocab.ex: A single neuron can connect with thousands of others.
vocab.exzh: 一個神經元可以和成千上萬個神經元相連。

vocab.ex: The traffic light gives a signal to stop.
vocab.exzh: 紅綠燈發出停止的訊號。

vocab.ex: The spinal cord runs down the middle of your backbone.
vocab.exzh: 脊髓沿著脊柱的中間往下延伸。

vocab.ex: Blinking when something flies at your face is a reflex.
vocab.exzh: 有東西飛向臉時眨眼，是一種反射。

vocab.ex: The goalkeeper reacted quickly and stopped the ball.
vocab.exzh: 守門員反應很快，擋下了球。

vocab.ex: Dogs have a much better sense of smell than people.
vocab.exzh: 狗的嗅覺比人好得多。

kinds_head.eyebrow: The Control Team · 指揮中心
kinds_head.en: Who does what in your nervous system
kinds_head.zh: 神經系統裡誰負責什麼

kinds.text_en: Its two halves cross over: the left half runs the right side of your body.
kinds.text_zh: 左右兩半是交叉的：左半邊管身體右側。

kinds.where_en: At the back, under the cerebrum
kinds.text_en: It fine-tunes every move, so you can ride a bike or carry a full bowl of soup.
kinds.text_zh: 它微調每個動作，讓你能騎腳踏車、端著一碗滿滿的湯。

kinds.where_en: Where the brain meets the spinal cord
kinds.text_en: Keeps you breathing, keeps your heart beating, and makes you swallow and cough, all without thinking.
kinds.text_zh: 讓你持續呼吸、心臟持續跳動，還負責吞嚥和咳嗽，完全不用想。

kinds.text_en: Carries messages between brain and body, and handles some reflexes all by itself.
kinds.text_zh: 在大腦和身體之間傳遞訊息，有些反射還能自己處理。

kinds.text_en: Sensory nerves bring news in; motor nerves carry orders out.
kinds.text_zh: 感覺神經把消息送進來，運動神經把命令送出去。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of it as a company: the cerebrum is the boss, the cerebellum is the coach, the brainstem runs the machines, and the spinal cord and nerves are the phone lines.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成一家公司：大腦是老闆，小腦是教練，腦幹負責顧機器，脊髓和神經是電話線。

measure.lead_en: Do the classic ruler test with a partner, then try the on-screen version below the model. Both turn how far the ruler falls into how long you took to react.
measure.lead_zh: 先和同伴做經典的直尺測驗，再試試模型下方的電腦版。兩者都是把尺掉的距離，換算成你反應所花的時間。

steps.en: Get ready
steps.zh: 準備
steps.text_en: Your partner holds a 30 cm ruler at the top. Put your thumb and finger open at the 0 mark, not touching it.
steps.text_zh: 同伴拿著一把 30 公分的尺的頂端；你的拇指和食指張開，對準 0 公分的位置，不要碰到。

steps.en: Drop and catch
steps.zh: 放手、接住
steps.text_en: Without warning, your partner lets go. Catch it as fast as you can and read the number at your fingers.
steps.text_zh: 同伴不預告地放手，你用最快的速度接住，讀出手指位置的刻度。

steps.en: Turn it into time
steps.zh: 換算成時間

myths.myth_en: We only use 10 percent of our brains.
myths.myth_zh: 我們只用了大腦的 10%。
myths.fact_en: Brain scans show that every part of the brain is active at some point during the day. Even during sleep, large parts of it are busy.
myths.fact_zh: 腦部掃描顯示，一天當中大腦的每個部位都會活躍。就連睡覺時，大腦的許多部分也在忙。

myths.myth_en: People are either left-brained or right-brained.
myths.myth_zh: 人分成「左腦型」和「右腦型」。
myths.fact_en: Each half does some jobs better, but healthy people use both halves together all the time. Studies have not found people who rely on one side more than the other.
myths.fact_zh: 左右腦各有比較擅長的工作，但健康的人隨時都是兩邊一起用。研究並沒有發現哪些人比較依賴某一邊。

myths.myth_en: Every movement you make is decided by your brain.
myths.myth_zh: 你的每個動作都是大腦決定的。
myths.fact_en: Reflexes, like pulling away from heat or the knee-jerk, are handled by the spinal cord before the brain even finds out.
myths.fact_zh: 反射動作，例如碰到燙的東西縮手、膝跳反射，是脊髓處理的，大腦都還來不及知道。

myths.myth_en: A bigger brain always means a smarter animal.
myths.myth_zh: 腦越大的動物越聰明。
myths.fact_en: A sperm whale's brain is about five times heavier than yours. What matters more is how the brain is built and how its cells are connected.
myths.fact_zh: 抹香鯨的腦大約比你的重五倍。更重要的是大腦的構造，以及腦細胞怎麼連結。

tricks.body_en: Senses send news in, the brain decides, and muscles act. A reflex skips the middle step.
tricks.body_zh: 感官把消息送進來、大腦決定、肌肉行動；反射跳過了中間那一步。

tricks.body_en: The two halves of the brain cross over. When you write with your right hand, your left brain is giving the orders.
tricks.body_zh: 左右腦是交叉的。你用右手寫字時，下命令的是左腦。

tricks.body_en: Hand to spinal cord and straight back again. The brain gets a copy of the message, but only afterward.
tricks.body_zh: 從手到脊髓，再直接回去。大腦也會收到訊息的副本，只是晚了一步。

tricks.body_en: The fastest nerve signals reach about 430 km/h; Taiwan's high-speed rail tops out at about 300 km/h.
tricks.body_zh: 最快的神經訊號約時速 430 公里；台灣高鐵最快約時速 300 公里。

materials.en: A 30 cm ruler for each pair
materials.zh: 每兩人一把 30 公分直尺

materials.en: A results table on the board
materials.zh: 黑板上的結果表

steps.en: Each student does five catches with the hand they write with and five with the other hand.
steps.zh: 每個人用寫字的手接五次，再用另一隻手接五次。

steps.en: Write down the distance each time and find the middle value.
steps.zh: 每次都記下距離，找出中間值。

steps.en: Do five more catches while counting backward from 100 by sevens out loud.
steps.zh: 再接五次，這次一邊大聲從 100 開始每次減 7 倒數。

steps.en: Compare: writing hand vs. other hand, and focused vs. distracted.
steps.zh: 比較：寫字的手 vs. 另一隻手、專心 vs. 分心。

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the distracted round is usually slower, which connects straight to the danger of using a phone while crossing the street. Use the conversion table in the Measure Yourself section, or the on-screen test, to turn centimeters into seconds.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：分心的那一輪通常比較慢，正好可以連結到邊滑手機邊過馬路的危險。用「親身測量」段落的換算表，或電腦版測驗，把公分換成秒數。

materials.en: Two blunt pencils held together with a rubber band, or an unbent paper clip with its two ends about 1 cm apart
materials.zh: 兩支鈍頭鉛筆用橡皮筋綁在一起，或把迴紋針扳開、兩端相距約 1 公分

materials.en: A partner and a blindfold or closed eyes
materials.zh: 一位同伴，閉上眼睛或蒙眼

steps.en: With your eyes closed, your partner gently touches your fingertip with either one point or both points.
steps.zh: 你閉上眼睛，同伴用一個點或兩個點輕輕碰你的指尖。

steps.en: Say “one” or “two.” Try ten times and count how many you get right.
steps.zh: 說出「一點」或「兩點」，試十次，算答對幾次。

steps.en: Repeat on the back of your hand and on your forearm.
steps.zh: 在手背和前臂上重複一次。

steps.en: Where could you tell two points apart most easily? Why might that be?
steps.zh: 哪裡最容易分辨出兩個點？為什麼？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: fingertips have many more touch sensors than the forearm, and a bigger area of the brain's touch map is given to them. Press gently, and never use sharp points.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：指尖的觸覺感受器比前臂多得多，大腦的觸覺地圖也分給它們比較大的區域。要輕輕地碰，絕對不要用尖銳的東西。

culture.title_en: Where the Word 神經 Came From
culture.body_en: The word for nerve, 神經 (shénjīng), was made up in Japan in 1774, when the doctor Sugita Genpaku translated a Dutch anatomy book. He joined 神, from 神氣 (spirit), with 經, from 經脈 (the body's channels in Chinese medicine), and the word later spread to Chinese. Everyday Chinese also talks about the brain with 腦筋: to think hard is 動腦筋, “move your brain sinews,” and a brain teaser is a 腦筋急轉彎, “a sharp turn for the brain.”
culture.body_zh: 「神經」這個詞是 1774 年在日本造出來的：醫師杉田玄白翻譯一本荷蘭解剖書時，取「神氣」的「神」和中醫「經脈」的「經」組成這個詞，後來才傳進中文。日常中文也用「腦筋」講大腦：用心思考叫「動腦筋」，猜謎題叫「腦筋急轉彎」。

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If you hit your head and feel dizzy, sick to your stomach, or very sleepy, tell an adult right away. Wear a helmet when you ride, and keep your phone away while crossing the street.

lessons.title: How Do Your Eyes See?
lessons.blurb_en: Light bends inside your eye and paints an upside-down picture at the back. Focus a 3D eye near and far, fix blurry vision with glasses, and find the blind spot in your own eye.
lessons.blurb_zh: 光在眼睛裡轉彎，在眼球後面畫出一幅上下顛倒的圖。讓 3D 眼睛看遠看近、戴上眼鏡修正模糊，再找出你自己眼睛裡的盲點。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your eye works like a camera. The cornea and the lens bend light to make a sharp, upside-down picture on the retina, and your brain turns it right side up. Where the optic nerve leaves the eye, there are no light-sensing cells, so every eye has a blind spot.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 眼睛就像一台相機：角膜和水晶體把光折彎，在視網膜上形成清楚、上下顛倒的像，大腦再把它轉正。視神經離開眼球的地方沒有感光細胞，所以每隻眼睛都有一個盲點。

lab.title_en: Follow the Light into Your Eye
lab.how_en: Pick something far or near, and watch light from its top and bottom cross inside the eye and land upside down on the retina. Turn the light up and down to see the pupil change, focus the lens yourself, then switch to a nearsighted or farsighted eye and put on glasses. The blind spot button shows where light goes when part of a picture disappears.
lab.how_zh: 選一個遠的或近的東西，看它上端和下端的光在眼睛裡交叉，上下顛倒地落在視網膜上。把光線調亮調暗，看瞳孔怎麼變；自己動手調水晶體對焦；再換成近視或遠視的眼睛，戴上眼鏡試試。按「盲點」，看看畫面有一部分消失時，光落到了哪裡。

legend.zh: 綠色的線：物體上端發出的光

legend.en: Pale spot: the blind spot, where the optic nerve leaves
legend.zh: 淡黃色的圓點：盲點，視神經離開眼球的地方

legend.en: Green glow: the vision area at the back of the brain

paras: Look up from this page at something far away, then look back down. Your eyes just changed their focus twice, and you probably did not even notice. Each eye is a ball about 2.4 centimeters across, filled with a clear jelly. Light bounces off everything around you, and some of it enters your eyes. Inside, the light is bent to make a tiny, sharp picture at the back of each eye, a lot like the picture inside a camera. Your eyes collect the light, but the seeing itself happens in your brain.

The front of the eye lets light in. First comes the cornea, a clear, curved window that does most of the bending of light. Behind it is the iris, the colored part of your eye, which is a ring of muscle. The black circle in the middle of the iris is the pupil, and it is simply a hole. In bright sunlight, the iris makes the pupil as small as 2 millimeters to keep out extra light. In the dark, it opens the pupil to about 8 millimeters to catch as much light as it can. When you walk into a dark movie theater, your pupils open wide in seconds, but your eyes need several more minutes to get used to the dark.

Behind the pupil is the lens, which fine-tunes the focus. A ring of tiny muscles around it changes its shape. To see something far away, the lens is pulled flatter. To see something up close, the muscles tighten and the lens gets rounder, so it bends light more. Light from each point of an object comes together at one point on the retina, the thin layer at the back of the eye. But here is a surprise: the picture on your retina is upside down and flipped left to right. Your brain sorts this out, so the world looks right side up.

The retina is where light turns into nerve signals. It has more than 120 million light-sensing cells of two kinds. Rods work in dim light but cannot see color, which is why things look gray at night. Cones need brighter light, and they let you see colors and fine details. The signals leave the eye through the optic nerve, a cable of about a million nerve fibers. Where the optic nerve leaves the eye, there are no light-sensing cells at all, so every eye has a blind spot. You never notice it, because your two eyes cover for each other and your brain fills in the gap.

Some eyes have trouble focusing. In a nearsighted eye, the eyeball is a little too long. Light from faraway things comes to a point in front of the retina, so the board at school looks blurry, but a book up close looks sharp. In a farsighted eye, the eyeball is a little too short, so things up close are harder to see clearly. Glasses fix both problems by bending the light a little before it enters the eye. Lenses for nearsighted eyes are thinner in the middle and spread the light out. Lenses for farsighted eyes are thicker in the middle and bring the light together.

Taiwan has one of the highest rates of nearsightedness in the world, and most students here are nearsighted by the end of elementary school. Scientists have found that children who spend more time outdoors are less likely to become nearsighted, which is why Taiwan encourages two hours outside every day. When you read or use a screen, keep it at least 30 centimeters away, and every 30 minutes, rest your eyes for 10 minutes by looking far away. Never look straight at the Sun. Now try the blind spot test below the model and find the hole in your own vision.
paras_zh: 從這一頁抬起頭，看看遠方的東西，再低頭看回來。你的眼睛剛剛換了兩次焦距，你大概完全沒注意到。每隻眼睛都是一顆直徑約 2.4 公分的球，裡面裝滿透明的膠狀物。光從身邊的每樣東西反射出來，其中一些進入你的眼睛。在眼睛裡，光被折彎，在每隻眼睛的後面形成一幅小小的、清楚的圖像，很像相機裡的影像。眼睛負責收集光，真正「看見」卻是在大腦裡發生的。
眼睛的前面負責讓光進來。最前面是角膜，一片透明、彎彎的窗戶，大部分的折光都是它做的。角膜後面是虹膜，就是眼睛有顏色的部分，它是一圈肌肉。虹膜中間的黑色圓圈是瞳孔，它其實只是一個洞。在明亮的陽光下，虹膜把瞳孔縮小到只有 2 毫米，擋掉多餘的光；在黑暗中，它把瞳孔張開到大約 8 毫米，盡量收集光線。走進漆黑的電影院時，瞳孔幾秒鐘就張大了，但眼睛還要再過好幾分鐘才能適應黑暗。
瞳孔後面是水晶體，負責微調焦距。它周圍有一圈很小的肌肉，可以改變它的形狀。要看遠方的東西，水晶體被拉得比較扁；要看近的東西，肌肉收緊，水晶體變得比較圓，把光折得更多。物體上每一點發出的光，會聚在視網膜上的一點；視網膜是眼睛後面薄薄的一層。不過有件令人驚訝的事：視網膜上的像是上下顛倒、左右相反的。大腦會把它整理好，所以你看到的世界是正的。
視網膜是光變成神經訊號的地方。它有超過一億兩千萬個感光細胞，分成兩種：桿狀細胞在昏暗的光線下工作，但看不出顏色，所以晚上東西看起來灰灰的；錐狀細胞需要比較亮的光，讓你看見顏色和細節。訊號經由視神經離開眼睛，視神經是一條大約有一百萬條神經纖維的電纜。視神經離開眼球的地方完全沒有感光細胞，所以每隻眼睛都有一個盲點。你從來沒注意到它，因為兩隻眼睛會互相補位，大腦也會把空缺補起來。
有些眼睛對焦有困難。近視的眼睛，眼球稍微太長，遠方東西的光在視網膜前面就聚成一點，所以教室的黑板看起來模模糊糊，近處的書卻很清楚。遠視的眼睛，眼球稍微太短，所以近的東西比較難看清楚。眼鏡在光進入眼睛之前先把它稍微折彎，兩種問題都能解決。近視的鏡片中間比較薄，把光散開；遠視的鏡片中間比較厚，把光聚攏。
台灣是全世界近視比率最高的地方之一，大多數學生到國小畢業時就已經近視了。科學家發現，在戶外待得比較久的孩子比較不容易近視，所以台灣鼓勵大家每天到戶外兩小時。看書或看螢幕時，至少保持 30 公分的距離，每看 30 分鐘就休息 10 分鐘，看看遠方。絕對不要直視太陽。現在試試模型下方的盲點測驗，找出你自己視野裡的那個洞。
questions: What do the cornea and the lens do?
Why does every eye have a blind spot?
Why can a nearsighted person read a book easily but not the board at school?
answers: They bend light so that it makes a sharp picture on the retina. The cornea does most of the bending, and the lens changes shape to focus on things near or far.
Where the optic nerve leaves the eye, there are no light-sensing cells, so light that lands on that spot is not seen.
A nearsighted eyeball is a little too long. Light from faraway things comes to a point in front of the retina, so they look blurry, but light from things up close comes to a point on the retina.

kinds_head.eyebrow: Parts of the Eye · 眼睛的構造
kinds_head.en: Who does what inside your eye

kinds.where_en: The clear window at the very front
kinds.text_en: It has no blood vessels, so it stays perfectly clear. It gets its oxygen straight from the air and from your tears.
kinds.text_zh: 它沒有血管，所以能保持完全透明；它直接從空氣和眼淚裡取得氧氣。

kinds.where_en: The colored ring and the hole in its middle
kinds.where_zh: 有顏色的圓環和中間的洞
kinds.control_en: Lets in the right amount of light
kinds.text_en: Brown, blue, green, or gray, the iris is a muscle that makes the pupil smaller in bright light and bigger in the dark.
kinds.text_zh: 不論是棕色、藍色、綠色還是灰色，虹膜都是肌肉：光亮時把瞳孔縮小，黑暗時把它張大。

kinds.text_en: Tiny muscles let it get rounder for things up close and flatter for things far away.
kinds.text_zh: 周圍的小肌肉讓它看近時變圓、看遠時變扁。

kinds.where_en: The thin layer at the back
kinds.text_en: More than 120 million rods and cones. The sharpest spot, the fovea, sits right where you are looking.
kinds.text_zh: 有超過一億兩千萬個桿狀與錐狀細胞；看得最清楚的中央小凹，就在你視線正對的地方。

kinds.where_en: Leaves the back of the eye
kinds.control_en: Carries the picture to the brain
kinds.text_en: About a million nerve fibers. Where it leaves the eye, there are no light-sensing cells: that is your blind spot.
kinds.text_zh: 大約一百萬條神經纖維。它離開眼球的地方沒有感光細胞，那就是你的盲點。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a camera: the cornea and the lens are the camera's lens, the pupil is the opening that lets light in, the retina is the image sensor, and the optic nerve is the cable to the computer, which is your brain.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把眼睛想成一台相機：角膜和水晶體是鏡頭，瞳孔是讓光進來的光圈，視網膜是感光元件，視神經是接到電腦的傳輸線，而那台電腦就是你的大腦。

measure.lead_en: Use the blind spot card below the model, or draw your own on paper: a small cross and a dot about 8 cm apart. Every eye has a blind spot. Here is how to catch yours.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的盲點測驗卡，或在紙上自己畫一張：一個小十字和一個圓點，相距大約 8 公分。每隻眼睛都有盲點，用下面的方法把它找出來。

steps.en: Close one eye
steps.zh: 閉上一隻眼睛
steps.text_en: Cover your right eye. With your left eye, stare at the cross. The dot should be on the left. To test your right eye, switch sides.
steps.text_zh: 遮住右眼，用左眼盯著十字，圓點應該在左邊。要測右眼，就左右對調。

steps.en: Move slowly
steps.zh: 慢慢移動
steps.text_en: Keep staring at the cross and slowly move your face closer or farther away. At one distance, usually 20 to 35 cm, the dot disappears!
steps.text_zh: 一直盯著十字，慢慢把臉靠近或拉遠。到了某個距離（通常是 20 到 35 公分），圓點就不見了！

steps.en: Do the math
steps.zh: 算一算
steps.text_en: Measure the gap between the cross and the dot, and your distance from the screen. Gap ÷ distance is usually about 0.27, which means your blind spot sits about 15° to the side.
steps.text_zh: 量出十字和圓點的距離，以及眼睛到螢幕的距離。兩者相除通常約 0.27，表示你的盲點在視線旁邊大約 15° 的地方。

myths.myth_en: If you cross your eyes, they might get stuck that way.
myths.myth_zh: 鬥雞眼做太久，眼睛會卡住回不來。
myths.fact_en: The muscles that move your eyes always relax again. Crossing your eyes may feel funny, but it cannot make them stay crossed.
myths.fact_zh: 控制眼球轉動的肌肉一定會再放鬆。故意鬥雞眼可能會怪怪的，但不會讓眼睛卡住。

myths.myth_en: Eating lots of carrots gives you super night vision.
myths.myth_zh: 多吃紅蘿蔔，晚上就能看得超清楚。
myths.fact_en: Carrots have vitamin A, which your eyes need, but extra carrots will not make healthy eyes better than normal. The story spread in Britain during World War II, partly to keep its new radar a secret.
myths.fact_zh: 紅蘿蔔含有眼睛需要的維生素 A，但多吃並不會讓健康的眼睛變得比正常更好。這個說法是二次大戰時在英國流傳開的，部分原因是為了掩護他們的新雷達。

myths.myth_en: Wearing glasses makes your eyes weaker.
myths.myth_zh: 戴眼鏡會讓眼睛越來越差。
myths.fact_en: Glasses do not change the shape of your eye. They only bend light so the picture lands on the retina. Many children's eyes keep changing as they grow, with or without glasses.
myths.fact_zh: 眼鏡不會改變眼球的形狀，它只是把光折彎，讓影像落在視網膜上。很多孩子的眼睛在成長中本來就會改變，戴不戴眼鏡都一樣。

myths.myth_en: You see with your eyes.
myths.myth_zh: 我們是用眼睛看東西的。
myths.fact_en: Your eyes only collect light. The seeing happens in your brain, which makes sense of the upside-down picture and fills in your blind spot.
myths.fact_zh: 眼睛只負責收集光，真正的「看見」發生在大腦：它把上下顛倒的影像整理好，還把盲點補起來。

tricks.body_en: The iris works like a camera's opening: small in sunlight, wide open in the dark.
tricks.body_zh: 虹膜就像相機的光圈：陽光下縮小，黑暗中張大。

tricks.title_en: Round for near, flat for far
tricks.body_en: To look at something close, tiny muscles tighten and the lens gets rounder. Looking far away lets them relax, and the lens flattens.
tricks.body_zh: 看近的東西時，小肌肉收緊，水晶體變圓；看遠方時肌肉放鬆，水晶體變扁。

tricks.body_en: Both start with C. Rods take over in dim light, which is why the world looks gray at night.
tricks.body_zh: 兩個字都是 C 開頭：錐狀細胞看顏色。光線暗時換桿狀細胞上場，所以晚上世界看起來灰灰的。

tricks.body_en: The eye makes an upside-down picture, and the brain sorts it out so you see the world right side up.
tricks.body_zh: 眼睛做出上下顛倒的像，大腦把它整理好，你看到的世界才是正的。

materials.en: A cardboard tube, such as a paper towel roll
materials.zh: 一個紙筒，例如廚房紙巾的捲筒

materials.en: Aluminum foil, a pin, wax paper, and two rubber bands
materials.zh: 鋁箔紙、一根大頭針、烘焙紙和兩條橡皮筋

materials.en: A jacket or a dark cloth
materials.zh: 一件外套或一塊深色的布

steps.en: Cover one end of the tube with foil and poke a tiny hole in the middle with the pin.
steps.zh: 用鋁箔紙蓋住紙筒的一端，用大頭針在中間戳一個小洞。

steps.en: Cover the other end with wax paper. This is your screen.
steps.zh: 用烘焙紙蓋住另一端，這就是你的屏幕。

steps.en: Point the foil end at a bright window or a lamp. Drape the jacket over your head and the screen end so it is dark.
steps.zh: 把鋁箔那一端對著明亮的窗戶或檯燈，用外套蓋住頭和屏幕那一端，讓它暗下來。

steps.en: Look at the screen. Is the picture right side up? Wave your hand in front of the window. Which way does it move?
steps.zh: 看看屏幕上的影像是正的嗎？在窗戶前揮揮手，影像往哪個方向動？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the pinhole is the pupil and the wax paper is the retina, and the picture is upside down, just like in your eye. Make the hole bigger and the picture gets brighter but blurrier. A real eye adds a lens, so its picture is bright and sharp at the same time. Never point the viewer at the Sun.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：針孔就是瞳孔，烘焙紙就是視網膜，影像和眼睛裡一樣是上下顛倒的。把洞戳大，影像會變亮但變模糊；真正的眼睛多了水晶體，所以影像能又亮又清楚。絕對不要把觀景器對著太陽。

materials.en: A partner
materials.zh: 一位同伴

materials.en: A normally lit room
materials.zh: 一間光線正常的教室

steps.en: Sit facing your partner and look at the size of their pupils.
steps.zh: 和同伴面對面坐，看看對方瞳孔的大小。

steps.en: Your partner covers both eyes with their hands for 20 seconds.
steps.zh: 同伴用雙手遮住兩隻眼睛 20 秒。

steps.en: When they take their hands away, watch closely: the big, dark pupils shrink in about a second.
steps.zh: 對方把手拿開時仔細看：又大又黑的瞳孔大約一秒內就縮小了。

steps.en: Next, your partner covers just one eye. Watch the open eye. Does its pupil change too?
steps.zh: 接著，同伴只遮住一隻眼睛，你觀察沒遮住的那一隻：它的瞳孔也有變化嗎？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the two pupils usually change together, because the brain controls them as a pair, so the open eye's pupil gets a little bigger too. Never shine a flashlight or a phone light into anyone's eyes.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：兩邊的瞳孔通常一起變化，因為大腦把它們當成一對來控制，所以沒遮的那隻眼睛，瞳孔也會稍微變大。絕對不要用手電筒或手機的燈照別人的眼睛。

culture.title_en: A Little Person in Your Eye
culture.body_en: Look closely into a friend's eye, and you will see a tiny picture of yourself. English and Chinese both noticed this. The English word pupil comes from the Latin pupilla, “little doll.” In Chinese, the pupil is 瞳孔 (tóngkǒng); the 童 in 瞳 mainly gives the sound, but the pupil is also called 瞳人 (tóngrén), “the person in the eye.” Chinese names the two focusing problems simply: 近視 (jìnshì), “near-seeing,” and 遠視 (yuǎnshì), “far-seeing.” And the saying 眼見為憑, “what the eyes see is proof,” may be worth a second thought once you have found your blind spot.
culture.body_zh: 仔細看朋友的眼睛，會看到一個小小的自己。英文和中文都注意到了這件事：英文的 pupil（瞳孔）來自拉丁文 pupilla，意思是「小娃娃」；中文的「瞳」，「童」主要是表音，不過瞳孔也叫「瞳人」，因為對看時瞳孔裡會映出人影。兩種對焦問題，中文說得很直白：「近視」看得清近的，「遠視」看得清遠的。至於「眼見為憑」這句話，找到自己的盲點之後，或許值得再想一想。

culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Never look straight at the Sun, even with sunglasses. If things suddenly look blurry, you see flashes or a dark shadow, or an eye hurts or gets hit, tell an adult right away. Have your eyes checked once a year.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。絕對不要直視太陽，戴太陽眼鏡也不行。如果看東西突然變模糊、看到閃光或一片黑影，或眼睛疼痛、被撞到，請馬上告訴大人。每年做一次視力檢查。

lessons.title: How Do Your Ears Hear?
lessons.blurb_en: Sound is air that shakes. Follow it through your eardrum and three tiny bones into a snail-shaped tube, and find the highest note you can still hear.
lessons.blurb_zh: 聲音是空氣在振動。跟著它穿過鼓膜和三塊小骨頭，走進蝸牛殼形狀的耳蝸，再找出你還聽得到的最高音。
lessons.big_idea_en: Sound is air shaking. Your eardrum catches the shaking, three tiny bones pass it on, and the cochlea turns it into nerve signals: high sounds near its entrance, low sounds deep inside.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 聲音是空氣在振動：鼓膜接住振動，三塊小骨頭把它傳下去，耳蝸再把它變成神經訊號——高音在入口附近，低音在最裡面。

lab.title_en: Follow a Sound into Your Ear
lab.how_en: Pick a sound, and watch the air shake its way down the ear canal, rock the three tiny bones, and light up the cochlea: high notes near the entrance, low notes at the tip. Change the pitch and the loudness, uncoil the cochlea to see the whole map, and spin around to see why you get dizzy. Then take the hearing test below the model.
lab.how_zh: 選一個聲音，看空氣的振動沿著耳道走進去，推動三塊小骨頭，讓耳蝸亮起來：高音在入口附近，低音在尖端。調整音高和音量，把耳蝸拉直看整張地圖，再轉個圈，看看為什麼會頭暈。最後做模型下方的聽力測驗。

legend.en: Blue dots: air shaking (slowed way down)
legend.zh: 藍色的點：振動的空氣（放得很慢）

legend.en: Ivory: the three tiny bones
legend.zh: 象牙色：三塊聽小骨

legend.en: Rainbow on the cochlea: where each pitch lands
legend.zh: 耳蝸上的彩虹：每個音高落在哪裡

legend.en: Glow: where this note bends the hair cells
legend.zh: 發亮的點：這個音讓毛細胞彎曲的位置

legend.en: Yellow: the hearing nerve to the brain
legend.zh: 黃色：通往大腦的聽神經

lab.scale_en: The skull is real, from the same BodyParts3D skeleton as Lesson 1; the ear is our own drawing, shown four times bigger than life and cut open. BodyParts3D has no ear bones, so we drew the hammer, anvil, and stirrup ourselves. The outer ear is drawn smaller than it would be at this size, and the air waves are slowed down so much that you can see them. Where each pitch lands along the cochlea follows the Greenwood formula used by hearing scientists.
lab.scale_zh: 頭骨是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架；耳朵是本站自繪的示意圖，放大成真實的四倍並且剖開。BodyParts3D 沒有聽小骨，所以鎚骨、砧骨、鐙骨是我們自己畫的。外耳畫得比這個比例該有的小，空氣的振動也放慢到眼睛看得見。每個音高在耳蝸上的位置，依照聽覺科學家使用的 Greenwood 公式。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright; the ear, the brain, and the sound waves are our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並轉正方向，耳朵、大腦與聲波為本站自繪示意。

paras: Clap your hands. The clap pushes the air, and the push travels outward in waves at about 340 meters per second, fast enough to cross a soccer field in a third of a second. When the waves reach you, the air in your ear shakes back and forth, and your ears turn that shaking into sound. Fast shaking sounds high, like a bird. Slow shaking sounds low, like a drum. Scientists count the shakes in hertz: one hertz means one shake every second. Young people can hear from about 20 to 20,000 hertz.

The part of your ear that you can see is shaped to catch sound and send it into the ear canal, a tube about 2.5 centimeters long. At the end of the canal is the eardrum, a thin, tight skin about as wide as your little fingernail. When sound waves hit it, the eardrum shakes, just like the skin of a drum. The canal also makes earwax, which traps dust and germs and slowly moves out on its own. That is why doctors say you should never push cotton swabs into your ears.

Behind the eardrum is a tiny space filled with air, and in it are the three smallest bones in your body: the hammer, the anvil, and the stirrup. They pass the shaking along like a lever and make it about twenty times stronger. The stirrup is only about 3 millimeters long, smaller than a grain of rice. A thin tube connects this space to the back of your nose. When your ears pop in an elevator or on an airplane, that tube has just opened to let air in or out.

The stirrup pushes on the cochlea, a tube rolled up like a snail shell and filled with liquid. Inside are about 15,000 hair cells, each topped with tiny hairs that bend when the liquid moves. High notes bend the hairs near the entrance of the cochlea, and low notes travel all the way to its tip. The bending makes nerve signals, which race along the hearing nerve to your brain. Each ear sends signals to both sides of the brain, and by comparing your two ears, your brain can tell which direction a sound came from.

Next to the cochlea are three loops filled with liquid, called the semicircular canals. They do not hear at all. Instead, they help you keep your balance. When you turn your head, the liquid in the loops sloshes and bends more hair cells, telling your brain which way you moved. If you spin around and stop suddenly, the liquid keeps swirling for a moment, so your brain thinks you are still turning. That is why you feel dizzy.

Hair cells cannot grow back once they are damaged, so loud sounds can harm your hearing for life. Loudness is measured in decibels. Talking is about 60 decibels, and busy traffic is about 85. Sounds that loud or louder can harm your hearing if you listen for a long time. Firecrackers at a temple festival can be louder than 120 decibels, so cover your ears or keep your distance. With earphones, keep the volume low and take breaks. Now try the hearing test below the model and find the highest note you can hear.
paras_zh: 拍一下手。這一拍推動了空氣，這股推力以每秒大約 340 公尺的速度一波波往外傳，三分之一秒就能跑過一座足球場。聲波到達你身邊時，耳朵裡的空氣前後振動，耳朵再把這種振動變成聲音。振動得快，聽起來就高，像鳥叫；振動得慢，聽起來就低，像鼓聲。科學家用「赫茲」計算振動的次數：一赫茲就是每秒振動一次。年輕人大約聽得到 20 到 20,000 赫茲。
耳朵露在外面的部分，形狀剛好能接住聲音，把它送進耳道。耳道是一條大約 2.5 公分長的管子，盡頭是鼓膜：一片又薄又緊的皮膜，大約和你的小指指甲一樣寬。聲波打到鼓膜時，鼓膜就像鼓皮一樣振動。耳道也會製造耳垢，耳垢能黏住灰塵和病菌，還會自己慢慢往外移，所以醫生說絕對不要把棉花棒往耳朵裡塞。
鼓膜後面是一個裝著空氣的小空間，裡面有全身最小的三塊骨頭：鎚骨、砧骨和鐙骨。它們像槓桿一樣把振動傳下去，還讓它增強大約二十倍。鐙骨只有大約 3 毫米長，比一粒米還小。有一條細細的管子把這個空間連到鼻子後面；搭電梯或坐飛機時耳朵「啵」一聲，就是這條管子打開，讓空氣進出。
鐙骨推動耳蝸。耳蝸是一條捲得像蝸牛殼的管子，裡面裝滿液體，有大約一萬五千個毛細胞，每個頂端都有細細的毛，液體一動，毛就會彎。高音讓耳蝸入口附近的毛彎曲，低音則一路傳到耳蝸的尖端。毛的彎曲產生神經訊號，沿著聽神經衝向大腦。每隻耳朵都把訊號送到大腦的左右兩邊，大腦比較兩隻耳朵聽到的，就能分辨聲音從哪個方向來。
耳蝸旁邊有三個裝著液體的圓環，叫做半規管。它們完全不負責聽，而是幫你保持平衡。你轉頭時，圓環裡的液體晃動，讓更多毛細胞彎曲，告訴大腦你往哪個方向動。如果你轉圈圈又突然停下來，液體還會繼續轉一下，大腦就以為你還在轉，所以你會覺得頭暈。
毛細胞一旦受傷就長不回來，所以太大的聲音可能讓聽力永遠受損。聲音的大小用「分貝」來量：說話大約 60 分貝，車多的馬路大約 85 分貝；這麼大聲或更大聲的聲音，聽久了就可能傷害聽力。廟會的鞭炮可能超過 120 分貝，要摀住耳朵或離遠一點。戴耳機時把音量調小，並且記得休息。現在試試模型下方的聽力測驗，找出你聽得到的最高音。
questions: What happens to your eardrum when sound waves reach it?
How does the cochlea tell high notes from low notes?
Why do you feel dizzy after you spin around?
answers: It shakes back and forth like the skin of a drum, and it passes the shaking on to the three tiny bones.
High notes bend the hair cells near the entrance of the cochlea, and low notes travel all the way to its tip.
The liquid in the semicircular canals keeps swirling after you stop, so your brain thinks you are still turning.

kinds_head.eyebrow: Parts of the Ear · 耳朵的構造
kinds_head.en: From the air to your brain

kinds.where_en: The part you can see, and a 2.5 cm tube
kinds.where_zh: 看得見的部分和 2.5 公分長的管子
kinds.text_en: Its curves catch sound and send it in. The canal makes earwax, which cleans itself out.
kinds.text_zh: 彎彎曲曲的形狀把聲音收進來；耳道會製造耳垢，耳垢自己會往外移。

kinds.where_en: At the end of the ear canal
kinds.text_en: A thin, tight skin about as wide as your little fingernail. It moves less than the width of an atom for the quietest sounds.
kinds.text_zh: 又薄又緊的皮膜，大約和小指指甲一樣寬；最小的聲音讓它移動的距離，比一個原子還小。

kinds.text_en: The hammer, anvil, and stirrup work like a lever and make the push about twenty times stronger.
kinds.text_zh: 鎚骨、砧骨、鐙骨像槓桿一樣，把推力放大大約二十倍。

kinds.where_en: Deep inside, in the inner ear
kinds.text_en: About 15,000 hair cells, with high notes at the entrance and low notes at the tip, like a piano rolled up.
kinds.text_zh: 大約一萬五千個毛細胞：高音在入口、低音在尖端，像一架捲起來的鋼琴。

kinds.where_en: Three loops next to the cochlea
kinds.text_en: They point in three directions, so together they can feel your head nod, shake, and tilt.
kinds.text_zh: 三個圓環朝三個方向，合起來就能感覺到點頭、搖頭和歪頭。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a relay race: the outer ear catches the sound, the eardrum and the three tiny bones pass the shaking along, and the cochlea hands it to the nerve as a signal for your brain.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成一場接力賽：外耳接住聲音，鼓膜和三塊小骨頭把振動往下傳，耳蝸再把它變成訊號，交給神經送到大腦。

measure.title_en: Find the highest note you can hear
measure.title_zh: 找出你聽得到的最高音
measure.lead_en: The hearing test below the model plays short, quiet notes, starting at 8,000 hertz and climbing higher. Do it in a quiet room with your device's speakers, not earphones.
measure.lead_zh: 模型下方的聽力測驗會播放短短的、小聲的音，從 8,000 赫茲開始一路往上。請在安靜的房間用裝置的喇叭做，不要戴耳機。

steps.en: Set the volume
steps.zh: 調好音量
steps.text_en: Play the 1,000 Hz test note and turn your device's volume down until the note is soft but clear. Do not use earphones.
steps.text_zh: 播放 1,000 赫茲的試聽音，把裝置的音量調小，調到聽起來輕輕的但清楚。不要戴耳機。

steps.en: Climb the notes
steps.zh: 一路往上
steps.text_en: Tap “I hear it” for each higher note. When you cannot hear a note anymore, tap “I can't.” Your score is the last note you heard.
steps.text_zh: 每聽到一個更高的音，就按「聽得到」；聽不到時按「聽不到」。最後一個聽得到的音，就是你的成績。

steps.en: Compare
steps.zh: 比一比
steps.text_en: Compare with your classmates and with adults. Young people can often hear above 17,000 Hz, and the top note goes down as people get older. Some speakers cannot play the very highest notes.
steps.text_zh: 和同學、大人比一比。年輕人常常聽得到 17,000 赫茲以上，年紀越大，聽得到的最高音越低。有些喇叭本身放不出最高的音。

myths.myth_en: You should clean inside your ears with cotton swabs.
myths.myth_zh: 應該用棉花棒把耳朵裡面清乾淨。
myths.fact_en: Earwax cleans itself out. Cotton swabs can push the wax deeper or even hurt the eardrum. Just wash the outside of your ears.
myths.fact_zh: 耳垢會自己往外移。棉花棒反而可能把耳垢推得更深，甚至戳傷鼓膜。洗耳朵外面就好。

myths.myth_en: Only old people lose their hearing.
myths.myth_zh: 只有老人才會聽力變差。
myths.fact_en: Loud sounds can damage hair cells at any age, and they never grow back. That is why it matters to protect your hearing now.
myths.fact_zh: 太大的聲音在任何年紀都可能傷害毛細胞，而且毛細胞長不回來，所以現在就要保護聽力。

myths.myth_en: In space, you could hear a rocket roar.
myths.myth_zh: 在太空中也聽得到火箭的轟隆聲。
myths.fact_en: Space is almost empty, with no air to shake, so sound cannot travel there. Astronauts talk to each other by radio.
myths.fact_zh: 太空幾乎是空的，沒有空氣可以振動，所以聲音傳不過去。太空人是用無線電互相說話的。

myths.myth_en: Your voice sounds the same to you as it does to everyone else.
myths.myth_zh: 你聽到的自己的聲音，和別人聽到的一樣。
myths.fact_en: You hear your own voice through the air and also through the bones of your head, which makes it sound deeper. That is why your voice sounds strange in a recording.
myths.fact_zh: 你聽自己說話，除了經過空氣，還會經過頭骨傳進來，所以聽起來比較低沉；這就是錄音裡的聲音聽起來怪怪的原因。

tricks.body_en: Think of a blacksmith and a horse rider: the hammer hits the anvil, and the rider's foot rests in the stirrup. That is their order from the eardrum inward.
tricks.body_zh: 想像鐵匠和騎士：鎚子敲在鐵砧上，騎士的腳踩在馬鐙裡。這就是它們從鼓膜往裡排的順序。

tricks.title_en: High at the door, low at the end
tricks.title_zh: 高音在門口，低音在盡頭
tricks.body_en: High notes bend hair cells near the entrance of the cochlea; low notes travel all the way to the tip.
tricks.body_zh: 高音讓耳蝸入口附近的毛細胞彎曲；低音一路走到尖端。

tricks.body_en: Count the seconds between the lightning and the thunder, then divide by 3. That is about how many kilometers away the storm is.
tricks.body_zh: 數一數閃電到雷聲之間有幾秒，再除以 3，大約就是雷雨離你幾公里。

tricks.body_en: A common rule of thumb: no more than 60 percent of the volume, for no more than 60 minutes at a time.
tricks.body_zh: 常見的簡單原則：音量不超過 60%，一次不超過 60 分鐘。

materials.en: Two paper cups
materials.zh: 兩個紙杯

materials.en: 3 to 5 meters of string, and two toothpicks
materials.zh: 3 到 5 公尺長的線和兩根牙籤

steps.en: Poke a small hole in the bottom of each cup. Push the string through and tie it to a toothpick inside the cup.
steps.zh: 在兩個杯底各戳一個小洞，把線穿過去，在杯子裡綁在牙籤上。

steps.en: Walk apart until the string is tight. One person talks into a cup, and the other listens.
steps.zh: 兩個人往後退，把線拉直。一個人對著杯子說話，另一個人聽。

steps.en: Now let the string go loose. Can you still hear?
steps.zh: 再把線放鬆，還聽得到嗎？

steps.en: Pinch the string in the middle while your partner talks. What happens?
steps.zh: 同伴說話時，用手指捏住線的中間，會發生什麼事？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: sound is shaking, and a tight string carries the shaking from one cup to the other. The bottom of the cup works like an eardrum. A loose or pinched string cannot pass the shaking along, just as a damaged eardrum or stiff ear bones make hearing harder.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：聲音就是振動，拉緊的線把振動從一個杯子傳到另一個杯子，杯底就像鼓膜。線鬆了或被捏住，振動就傳不過去，就像鼓膜受傷或聽小骨變僵硬時，聽力會變差。

activities.title_en: Where Did That Sound Come From?

materials.en: A blindfold, or just closed eyes
materials.zh: 一條蒙眼布，或直接閉上眼睛

materials.en: A chair in the middle of the room
materials.zh: 教室中間的一張椅子

steps.en: One student sits in the chair with eyes closed.
steps.zh: 一位同學閉上眼睛坐在椅子上。

steps.en: Classmates take turns snapping their fingers from different places around the chair. The student points to where each sound came from.
steps.zh: 其他同學輪流在椅子周圍不同的地方彈手指，坐著的同學指出聲音從哪裡來。

steps.en: Now the student covers one ear with a hand and tries again.
steps.zh: 接著讓坐著的同學用手摀住一隻耳朵，再試一次。

steps.en: Count how many times they pointed the right way, with two ears and with one.
steps.zh: 算一算用兩隻耳朵和一隻耳朵時，各指對了幾次。

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: your brain finds a sound's direction by comparing the two ears: the sound reaches the nearer ear a tiny bit sooner and a little louder. With one ear covered, the guesses usually get much worse. Sounds straight in front or straight behind are the hardest.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：大腦比較兩隻耳朵來判斷方向：聲音會比較早、比較大聲地到達比較近的那隻耳朵。摀住一隻耳朵後，通常會猜錯得多。正前方和正後方的聲音最難分辨。

culture.body_en: In Chinese, 聰明 (cōngmíng) means smart, but the two characters began with the senses: 耳聰目明, ears that hear clearly and eyes that see clearly. Look closely, and 聰 has 耳, the character for ear, on its left side. Confucius said that by sixty, his ears were “in tune” (六十而耳順): he could listen to anything calmly. And 耳濡目染, “what the ears soak up and the eyes take in,” means learning from what you hear and see every day, which is a great way to learn English, too.
culture.body_zh: 中文的「聰明」是指頭腦好，但這兩個字原本講的是感官：「耳聰目明」，耳朵聽得清楚、眼睛看得明白。仔細看，「聰」字的左邊就是「耳」。孔子說自己「六十而耳順」，到了六十歲，聽什麼都能心平氣和。還有「耳濡目染」：每天聽到、看到的東西，不知不覺就學會了——這也是學英文的好方法。

culture.link_zh: 到中醫養生系列看更多

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. Do not put anything into your ear canal. If you have ear pain, ringing in your ears, or trouble hearing, tell an adult. Keep earphones at a low volume, and cover your ears near firecrackers.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。不要把任何東西放進耳道。如果耳朵痛、耳鳴，或聽不清楚，請告訴大人。戴耳機時音量要小，靠近鞭炮時要摀住耳朵。

lessons.title: What Does Your Skin Do?
lessons.blurb_en: Your skin is your biggest organ: it keeps germs out, feels the world, and cools you with sweat. Zoom into a slice of skin, and find out how strong today's sun is.
lessons.blurb_zh: 皮膚是身體最大的器官：擋住病菌、感覺世界、用汗幫你降溫。放大看一片皮膚，再算算今天的太陽有多強。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your skin is a living, waterproof wrap. It keeps germs out, feels touch, heat, and pain, cools you with sweat, and makes vitamin D in sunlight, but too much sun burns it.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 皮膚是活的防水外衣：擋住病菌、感覺碰觸冷熱與痛、用汗降溫、在陽光下製造維生素 D；但曬太多會灼傷。

lab.how_en: A tiny square of skin from your forearm, blown up 25 times and cut open. Pick a moment: a hot day, a cold wind, a light touch, or an hour in the sun, and watch the sweat glands, hairs, blood vessels, touch sensors, and pigment cells go to work. Then check how strong the sun in Changhua is today with the tool below the model.
lab.how_zh: 從前臂取下一小塊皮膚，放大 25 倍、剖開來看。選一個情境：大熱天、冷風、輕輕一碰，或曬一小時太陽，看汗腺、毛髮、血管、觸覺感受器和色素細胞怎麼工作。再用模型下方的小工具，看看今天彰化的太陽有多強。

legend.en: Tan top layer: epidermis
legend.zh: 最上面的米色層：表皮

legend.en: Pink middle layer: dermis
legend.zh: 中間的粉紅層：真皮

legend.en: Yellow bottom layer: fat
legend.zh: 最下面的黃色層：皮下脂肪

legend.en: Blue: sweat glands and sweat
legend.zh: 藍色：汗腺與汗水

legend.en: Yellow lines: nerves from the touch sensors
legend.zh: 黃色的線：觸覺感受器的神經

lab.scale_en: The forearm bones are real, from the same BodyParts3D skeleton as Lesson 1; the skin is our own drawing, shown 25 times bigger than life. The top layer is drawn thicker than it really is, and real skin has many more hairs, glands, and sensors packed into a space this size. The sun tool estimates the UV index for a clear sky; clouds, haze, and shade lower it.
lab.scale_zh: 前臂的骨頭是真實的，和第一課同一副 BodyParts3D 骨架；皮膚是本站自繪的示意圖，放大成真實的 25 倍。表皮畫得比真實的厚，而且真實皮膚在這麼小的範圍裡，毛髮、腺體和感受器多得多。太陽小工具估算的是晴天的紫外線指數；有雲、霾或遮蔽時會比較低。
lab.credit_html: Bone models: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC BY 4.0. We selected the bones, simplified the shapes, and turned the model upright; the skin is our own drawing. · 骨骼模型來源：BodyParts3D（日本生命科學資料庫中心，CC BY 4.0 授權）；本站挑選骨頭、簡化形狀並轉正方向，皮膚為本站自繪示意。

hot.text_en: Your sweat glands pour sweat out through tiny pores. As the sweat evaporates, it carries heat away. Blood vessels near the surface widen, so more warm blood can give off heat, which is why your face turns red.
hot.text_zh: 汗腺把汗水從小小的毛孔送出來；汗水蒸發時把熱帶走。靠近表面的血管變寬，讓更多溫暖的血散熱，所以臉會變紅。

cold.text_en: Tiny muscles pull each hair upright and make goosebumps. Furry animals trap warm air this way; for people it helps only a little. Blood vessels near the surface narrow to keep warm blood deeper inside.
cold.text_zh: 小小的肌肉把每根毛拉直，起了雞皮疙瘩。毛很多的動物靠這樣留住暖空氣，對人只有一點點幫助。靠近表面的血管變窄，把溫暖的血留在比較深的地方。

touch.text_en: Touch sensors near the top feel a light touch, and onion-shaped sensors deep down feel a hard press. They send signals along nerves to your spinal cord and brain in a few hundredths of a second.
touch.text_zh: 靠近表面的觸覺感受器感覺輕輕的碰觸，深處像洋蔥的感受器感覺用力的按壓。它們沿著神經把訊號送到脊髓和大腦，只要百分之幾秒。

sun.text_en: Ultraviolet light gets into the skin. The skin uses some of it to make vitamin D, and pigment cells make more melanin, a dark shield that shows up as a tan. Too much UV damages the cells and causes a sunburn.
sun.text_zh: 紫外線進入皮膚。皮膚用一部分紫外線製造維生素 D，色素細胞做出更多黑色素：一層深色的盾牌，看起來就是曬黑。紫外線太多會傷害細胞，造成曬傷。

paras: Your skin is your body's biggest organ. Spread out flat, an adult's skin would cover about 2 square meters, about the size of a single bed. It is waterproof, it stretches, and it repairs itself when you get a scrape. Most importantly, it is a wall that keeps germs, dirt, and harmful chemicals outside your body, and it keeps the water inside your body from drying out.

Skin has three layers. The top layer, the epidermis, is thinner than a sheet of paper on most of your body. Its outside is made of flat, dead cells that flake off all the time, and new cells from below replace the whole layer about once a month. Under it is the dermis, a thicker, stretchy layer that holds blood vessels, nerves, sweat glands, and the roots of your hairs. At the bottom is a layer of fat that works like a cushion and a warm blanket.

Skin also helps control your temperature. You have between 2 and 4 million sweat glands. On a hot day, they pour sweat onto your skin, and as the sweat evaporates, it carries heat away. The blood vessels near the surface also widen to let heat out, which is why you look red after running. When you are cold, those blood vessels narrow, and tiny muscles pull your hairs upright, giving you goosebumps.

Your skin is full of sensors. Some feel a light touch, some feel a hard press, and others feel heat, cold, itching, and pain. Your fingertips and lips have the most, which is why you read with your fingertips when you feel for something in the dark. Your fingertips also have ridges called fingerprints. They formed before you were born, and no two people have the same ones, not even identical twins.

Sunlight is good for skin in small amounts, because skin uses it to make vitamin D, which you need for strong bones. But sunlight also carries ultraviolet light, or UV, which you cannot see. To protect itself, skin makes a dark substance called melanin, and a tan is a sign that your skin has already been harmed by UV. Too much UV causes sunburn, and over many years it can lead to wrinkles and skin cancer.

Scientists measure the strength of UV with the UV index. When it is 3 or higher, you need protection, and in Taiwan it often goes above 10 on summer days around noon. A simple test: if your shadow is shorter than you are, the sun is strong. Wear a hat, cover up, look for shade, and use sunscreen. Now check how strong the sun is in Changhua today with the tool below the model.
paras_zh: 皮膚是身體最大的器官。把一個大人的皮膚攤平，大約有 2 平方公尺，差不多是一張單人床那麼大。它防水、有彈性，擦傷了還會自己修補。最重要的是，它像一道牆，把病菌、髒東西和有害的化學物質擋在身體外面，也讓身體裡的水分不會乾掉。
皮膚有三層。最上面一層是表皮，身體大部分地方的表皮比一張紙還薄。表皮的外面是扁平的死細胞，一直在剝落，下面長出來的新細胞大約一個月就把整層換新。表皮下面是真皮，比較厚、有彈性，裡面有血管、神經、汗腺和毛髮的根。最底下是一層脂肪，像坐墊也像保暖的毯子。
皮膚也幫忙控制體溫。你有兩百萬到四百萬個汗腺。大熱天時，汗腺把汗水送到皮膚上，汗水蒸發時把熱帶走。靠近表面的血管也會變寬讓熱散出去，所以跑步之後臉紅紅的。覺得冷的時候，這些血管會變窄，小小的肌肉把毛拉直，就起了雞皮疙瘩。
皮膚裡到處都是感受器：有的感覺輕輕的碰觸，有的感覺用力的按壓，還有的感覺熱、冷、癢和痛。指尖和嘴唇最多，所以在黑暗中找東西時，你會用指尖去摸。指尖還有一條條的紋路，叫做指紋。指紋在你出生以前就形成了，每個人都不一樣，連同卵雙胞胎也不同。
少量的陽光對皮膚有好處，因為皮膚會用它製造維生素 D，那是骨骼強壯需要的。但陽光也帶著看不見的紫外線。為了保護自己，皮膚會製造一種深色的物質，叫做黑色素；曬黑其實表示皮膚已經被紫外線傷害了。紫外線太多會曬傷，長年下來還可能造成皺紋和皮膚癌。
科學家用「紫外線指數」來量紫外線的強度。指數 3 以上就需要防護；在台灣，夏天中午前後常常超過 10。有個簡單的測試：如果你的影子比你的身高短，太陽就很強。戴帽子、穿長袖、找陰涼的地方、擦防曬乳。現在用模型下方的小工具，看看今天彰化的太陽有多強。
questions: What are the three layers of the skin?
How does sweat help you cool down?
Why is a tan not a sign of healthy skin?
answers: The epidermis on top, the dermis in the middle, and a layer of fat at the bottom.
Sweat comes out onto the skin, and as it evaporates, it carries heat away from your body.
Skin makes melanin to protect itself from UV, so a tan shows that the skin has already been harmed by UV.

vocab.ex: A baby's skin is very soft.
vocab.exzh: 嬰兒的皮膚非常柔軟。

vocab.ex: Wear a few thin layers when it is cold.
vocab.exzh: 天氣冷的時候，穿幾件薄的衣服一層層疊起來。

vocab.ex: We all sweat a lot after basketball practice.
vocab.exzh: 籃球練習之後，我們都流了很多汗。

vocab.ex: A helmet protects your head.
vocab.exzh: 安全帽保護你的頭。

vocab.ex: That scary story gave me goosebumps.
vocab.exzh: 那個恐怖故事讓我起雞皮疙瘩。

vocab.ex: I got a bad sunburn at the beach.
vocab.exzh: 我在海邊曬傷得很嚴重。

vocab.exzh: 出門前先擦防曬乳。

vocab.exzh: 警察在玻璃杯上找到一枚指紋。

kinds_head.eyebrow: Inside Your Skin · 皮膚的構造
kinds_head.zh: 三層皮膚和它們的幫手

kinds.text_en: Flat, dead cells on the outside flake off all the time. Pigment cells at its base make melanin.
kinds.text_zh: 外面扁平的死細胞一直在剝落；底部的色素細胞製造黑色素。

kinds.text_en: Holds blood vessels, nerves, sweat glands, and hair roots, all packed into stretchy fibers.
kinds.text_zh: 有彈性的纖維裡，塞滿了血管、神經、汗腺和毛髮的根。

kinds.text_en: Soft fat cushions bumps, keeps you warm, and stores energy.
kinds.text_zh: 軟軟的脂肪緩衝撞擊、保暖，還能儲存能量。

kinds.where_en: Coiled tubes deep in the dermis
kinds.where_zh: 真皮深處捲起來的小管子
kinds.text_en: Two to four million of them. Sweat cools you as it evaporates from your skin.
kinds.text_zh: 有兩百萬到四百萬個。汗水從皮膚蒸發時幫你降溫。

kinds.text_en: Different sensors feel light touch, pressure, heat, cold, itching, and pain. Fingertips have the most.
kinds.text_zh: 不同的感受器分別感覺輕觸、壓力、熱、冷、癢和痛；指尖最多。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a house: the epidermis is the roof, the dermis is the walls with all the pipes and wires inside, and the fat layer is the insulation under the floor.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把皮膚想成一棟房子：表皮是屋頂，真皮是牆壁，裡面藏著水管和電線，皮下脂肪則是地板下的隔熱層。

measure.lead_en: The sun tool below the model works out how high the sun is over Changhua at any time today and estimates the UV index for a clear sky. Then go outside and check with your own shadow.
measure.lead_zh: 模型下方的太陽小工具會算出今天任何時刻太陽在彰化有多高，並估算晴天的紫外線指數。再到戶外用自己的影子確認一下。

steps.en: Check the number
steps.zh: 看看指數
steps.text_en: Look at today's UV index chart. Find the hours when it is 3 or higher: those are the hours when you need protection.
steps.text_zh: 看今天的紫外線指數圖，找出指數 3 以上的時段：那些時候就需要防護。

steps.en: Measure your shadow
steps.zh: 量量你的影子
steps.text_en: At recess, stand in the sun and have a partner mark the end of your shadow. If your shadow is shorter than you are tall, the sun is strong.
steps.text_zh: 下課時站在太陽下，請同伴在你影子的尾端做記號。如果影子比你的身高短，太陽就很強。

steps.en: Compare
steps.zh: 比一比
steps.text_en: Compare with the UV forecast from Taiwan's Central Weather Administration. Clouds and haze usually make the real number lower than our clear-sky estimate.
steps.text_zh: 和中央氣象署的紫外線預報比一比。有雲或霾的時候，實際的數字通常比我們估算的晴天數字低。

myths.myth_en: You can't get sunburned on a cloudy day.
myths.myth_zh: 陰天不會曬傷。
myths.fact_en: Most UV passes through light clouds. You can get burned on a cloudy day, especially around noon in summer.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分的紫外線能穿過薄雲。陰天一樣會曬傷，尤其是夏天的中午前後。

myths.myth_en: A tan means your skin is healthy.
myths.myth_zh: 曬黑代表皮膚很健康。
myths.fact_en: A tan is your skin's way of protecting itself after UV has already damaged it.
myths.fact_zh: 曬黑是皮膚在被紫外線傷害之後，努力保護自己的結果。

myths.myth_en: Sweat itself smells bad.
myths.myth_zh: 汗本身就很臭。
myths.fact_en: Fresh sweat has almost no smell. The smell comes from bacteria on your skin breaking the sweat down.
myths.fact_zh: 剛流出來的汗幾乎沒有味道；臭味是皮膚上的細菌分解汗水產生的。

myths.myth_en: Goosebumps keep people warm.
myths.myth_zh: 雞皮疙瘩能讓人保暖。
myths.fact_en: In furry animals, raised fur traps a layer of warm air. People have so little body hair that goosebumps help only a little.
myths.fact_zh: 毛很多的動物把毛豎起來，可以留住一層暖空氣；人的體毛太少，雞皮疙瘩只能幫一點點忙。

tricks.body_en: If your shadow is shorter than you are, the sun is high and its UV is strong.
tricks.body_zh: 影子比身高短，表示太陽很高，紫外線很強。

tricks.body_en: A famous sun-safety rule from Australia: slip on a shirt, slop on sunscreen, slap on a hat.
tricks.body_zh: 澳洲有名的防曬口號：穿上衣服、擦上防曬乳、戴上帽子。

tricks.body_en: The epidermis sits on top of the dermis. Derma is Greek for skin.
tricks.body_zh: epidermis（表皮）在 dermis（真皮）的上面；derma 是希臘文的「皮膚」。

tricks.body_en: Sweat cools you only when it evaporates. Dripping sweat that just falls off does not help much.
tricks.body_zh: 汗水要蒸發才會帶走熱；直接滴下來的汗幫助不大。

materials.en: A soft pencil and a sheet of paper
materials.zh: 一支軟芯鉛筆和一張紙

materials.en: Clear tape and a magnifying glass
materials.zh: 透明膠帶和一個放大鏡

steps.en: Rub the pencil hard on the paper to make a dark patch.
steps.zh: 用鉛筆在紙上用力塗出一塊黑黑的區域。

steps.en: Rub your fingertip on the patch, then press a piece of tape onto your fingertip.
steps.zh: 用指尖在黑色區域上抹一抹，再把一段膠帶貼在指尖上。

steps.en: Peel off the tape and stick it on white paper. Look at it with the magnifying glass.
steps.zh: 把膠帶撕下來貼在白紙上，用放大鏡看。

steps.en: Is it a loop, a whorl, or an arch? Count each kind in the class.
steps.zh: 它是箕形、斗形還是弓形？統計全班每種各有幾個。

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: loops are the most common pattern, then whorls, and arches are the rarest. Even identical twins have different fingerprints, because tiny differences in the womb shape the ridges.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：箕形最常見，其次是斗形，弓形最少。連同卵雙胞胎的指紋都不一樣，因為在媽媽肚子裡的小小差異，就會影響紋路的形成。

materials.en: Two thermometers, or just your two hands
materials.zh: 兩支溫度計，或直接用兩隻手

materials.en: A wet paper towel and a fan or a piece of cardboard
materials.zh: 一張濕紙巾，以及電風扇或一塊紙板

steps.en: Wrap a wet paper towel around the end of one thermometer. Leave the other one dry.
steps.zh: 用濕紙巾包住一支溫度計的末端，另一支保持乾的。

steps.en: Fan both thermometers for three minutes.
steps.zh: 對兩支溫度計搧風三分鐘。

steps.en: Read both temperatures. Which one is cooler?
steps.zh: 讀出兩支的溫度，哪一支比較低？

steps.en: No thermometers? Wet the back of one hand, then blow on both hands. Which feels cooler?
steps.zh: 沒有溫度計？把一隻手的手背弄濕，再對兩隻手吹氣，哪一隻覺得比較涼？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the wet one cools down because evaporating water carries heat away, just like sweat. On a humid day, sweat evaporates slowly, which is why sticky summer days in Taiwan feel so hot.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：濕的那一支溫度比較低，因為水蒸發時把熱帶走，就像汗水一樣。潮濕的日子汗水不容易蒸發，所以台灣悶熱的夏天特別難受。

culture.body_en: English says goosebumps, and Chinese says 雞皮疙瘩 (jīpí gēda), “chicken-skin bumps.” Both languages compared our cold skin to a plucked bird. The classic 《孝經》 (Classic of Filial Piety) begins with a line many Taiwanese students know: 身體髮膚，受之父母 (shēntǐ fàfū, shòu zhī fùmǔ), “your body, hair, and skin come from your parents,” so taking care of them is the first way to show respect. Hats and sunscreen count!
culture.body_zh: 英文說 goosebumps（鵝的疙瘩），中文說「雞皮疙瘩」：兩種語言都把冷到起疙瘩的皮膚，比作拔了毛的鳥。《孝經》開頭有一句很多台灣學生都背過：「身體髮膚，受之父母，不敢毀傷，孝之始也。」好好照顧自己的身體和皮膚，就是孝順的開始——戴帽子、擦防曬也算喔！

lessons.title: Why Do We Get Two Sets of Teeth?
lessons.blurb_en: Baby teeth hold the place while adult teeth grow inside your jaw. Slide from age 3 to 20 and watch them trade places, then count your own teeth.
lessons.blurb_zh: 乳牙先占位置，恆牙在頷骨裡慢慢長。把年齡從 3 歲拉到 20 歲，看它們換班，再數數你自己的牙。
lessons.big_idea_en: Baby teeth hold the place while adult teeth grow inside your jaw. From about age 6 to 12, twenty baby teeth fall out and up to thirty-two adult teeth take over, and you only get one adult set.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 乳牙先占位置，恆牙在頷骨裡長大。大約 6 到 12 歲，20 顆乳牙一顆顆掉，最多 32 顆恆牙接班，而恆牙只有這一套。

lab.how_en: Slide the age from 3 to 20. White baby teeth fall out one by one, while ivory adult teeth climb up out of the jaw bone to take their place, and the big molars arrive at the back. Tap any tooth to see its name and when it usually comes in. Then use the tooth chart below the model to count your own teeth.
lab.how_zh: 把年齡從 3 歲拉到 20 歲：白色的乳牙一顆顆掉落，象牙色的恆牙從頷骨裡往上長出來接班，後面的大臼齒也一顆顆報到。點任何一顆牙，看它的名字和大約幾歲長出來。再用模型下方的牙齒圖，數數你自己的牙。

Every child is different: the ages in the model are typical averages from dental charts, and a year or two early or late is normal. The jaw itself also grows a lot during childhood, which the model does not show.

paras: Smile in a mirror and count your teeth. Most children have all 20 of their baby teeth by about age 3. Starting around age 6, the baby teeth fall out one by one, and adult teeth take their place. By about age 12 or 13, most children have lost all of their baby teeth. An adult can have up to 32 teeth, but there is no third set. Adult teeth have to last for the rest of your life.

Baby teeth are not just for practice. They help you chew and speak clearly, and they hold space in your jaw for the adult teeth. The adult teeth have been growing inside your jaw bone for years, right under the baby teeth. As an adult tooth moves up, the roots of the baby tooth above it slowly melt away. That is why a loose baby tooth has almost no root when it finally falls out.

Different teeth do different jobs. The flat incisors at the front bite and cut, like scissors. The pointed canines next to them grip and tear. The premolars and molars at the back have wide, bumpy tops for grinding food into a mash. Your first adult molars come in around age 6, behind the baby teeth, without pushing any baby tooth out, so many people do not even notice them. They are called six-year molars.

A tooth has layers. The outside is enamel, the hardest substance in your body. Under it is dentin, which is softer and a little yellow, and in the center is the pulp, which has nerves and blood vessels. The roots hold the tooth tightly in the jaw bone. Teeth are hard like bones, but they are not bones: a broken bone can heal, but enamel cannot grow back, so a hole in a tooth stays a hole until a dentist fills it.

Cavities start with bacteria that live on your teeth in a sticky film called plaque. When you eat sugar, the bacteria eat it too and make acid, which slowly dissolves the enamel. If the hole reaches the dentin and then the pulp, the tooth can really hurt. Fluoride helps enamel stay strong and can even repair the very earliest damage, which is why most toothpaste has fluoride in it.

Brush for two minutes, twice a day, with fluoride toothpaste, and clean between your teeth. In Taiwan, elementary students rinse with a fluoride mouthwash at school once a week, and first and second graders can get sealants: a thin coating that fills the deep grooves of the six-year molars, where food likes to hide. Eat fewer sweets and sugary drinks, and see a dentist every six months. Now count your own teeth with the tooth chart below the model.
paras_zh: 對著鏡子笑一笑，數數你的牙齒。大多數孩子大約 3 歲時就長齊 20 顆乳牙。從 6 歲左右開始，乳牙一顆顆掉落，恆牙接著長出來。大約 12、13 歲時，多數孩子的乳牙都換完了。大人最多可以有 32 顆牙，但是沒有第三套：恆牙要用一輩子。
乳牙可不只是拿來練習的。它們幫你咀嚼、讓你說話清楚，還在頷骨裡幫恆牙保留位置。恆牙早就在頷骨裡長了好幾年，就在乳牙的正下方。恆牙往上移動時，上面那顆乳牙的牙根會慢慢被吸收掉，所以搖搖欲墜的乳牙掉下來時，幾乎已經沒有牙根了。
不同的牙齒做不同的工作。前面扁扁的門牙負責咬斷、切開，像剪刀一樣；旁邊尖尖的犬齒負責抓住、撕開；後面的小臼齒和大臼齒頂端寬寬的、凹凸不平，負責把食物磨碎。第一顆恆牙大臼齒大約 6 歲時長在乳牙的後面，不會把任何乳牙推掉，所以很多人根本沒注意到它，大家叫它「六歲臼齒」。
牙齒是一層一層的。最外面是琺瑯質，是全身最堅硬的物質；下面是比較軟、帶點黃色的象牙質；中間是牙髓，裡面有神經和血管。牙根把牙齒牢牢固定在頷骨裡。牙齒和骨頭一樣硬，但牙齒不是骨頭：骨頭斷了會癒合，琺瑯質卻長不回來，所以牙齒上的洞會一直是個洞，直到牙醫把它補起來。
蛀牙是從住在牙齒上的細菌開始的，它們藏在一層黏黏的薄膜裡，叫做牙菌斑。你吃糖的時候，細菌也跟著吃，並且產生酸，酸會慢慢溶解琺瑯質。洞如果深到象牙質、再到牙髓，牙齒就會很痛。氟能讓琺瑯質保持堅固，甚至能修補最早期的損傷，所以大部分的牙膏都含氟。
每天刷牙兩次、每次兩分鐘，使用含氟牙膏，也要清潔牙縫。在台灣，國小學生每週在學校用含氟漱口水漱口一次，一、二年級的學生還可以做窩溝封填：用一層薄薄的材料填平六歲臼齒上深深的溝，那裡最容易卡食物。少吃甜食、少喝含糖飲料，每六個月看一次牙醫。現在用模型下方的牙齒圖，數數你自己的牙。

kinds_head.eyebrow: Kinds of Teeth · 牙齒的種類

kinds.text_en: 8 in both the baby set and the adult set. They are usually the first teeth to fall out, around age 6 or 7.
kinds.text_zh: 乳牙和恆牙都是 8 顆；通常最先掉，大約 6、7 歲。

kinds.text_en: 4 in each set. Their roots are the longest of all your teeth.
kinds.text_zh: 每一套 4 顆；它們的牙根是所有牙齒裡最長的。

kinds.where_en: Between the canines and the molars
kinds.text_en: Adults only: 8 premolars grow in where the baby molars were, at about ages 10 to 12.
kinds.text_zh: 只有恆牙有：8 顆小臼齒大約 10 到 12 歲時，長在原本乳臼齒的位置。

kinds.text_en: The six-year molars come in behind the baby teeth, and the twelve-year molars come in behind those.
kinds.text_zh: 六歲臼齒長在乳牙後面，十二歲臼齒再長在它們後面。

kinds.text_en: Up to 4, coming in between about 17 and 25, if at all. Some people never get them.
kinds.text_zh: 最多 4 顆，大約 17 到 25 歲才長；有些人一輩子都沒有。

lessons.kinds_note_en: A baby set has 8 incisors, 4 canines, and 8 molars: 20 teeth. An adult set adds 8 premolars and 4 more molars, plus up to 4 wisdom teeth: up to 32.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 一套乳牙有 8 顆門牙、4 顆犬齒、8 顆臼齒，共 20 顆。恆牙多了 8 顆小臼齒和 4 顆大臼齒，再加上最多 4 顆智齒，最多 32 顆。

measure.title_en: Count your teeth and find your tooth age
measure.title_zh: 數一數牙齒，算出牙齒年齡
measure.lead_en: Use a mirror and the tooth chart below the model. Tap each spot to mark a baby tooth, an adult tooth, or a gap, and the chart works out about how old your teeth look.
measure.lead_zh: 準備一面鏡子，搭配模型下方的牙齒圖。點每個位置，標出乳牙、恆牙或空位，牙齒圖會算出你的牙齒大約像幾歲。

steps.en: Look in a mirror
steps.zh: 照鏡子
steps.text_en: Wash your hands, smile wide, and look at one side at a time. New adult front teeth are bigger and often have little bumps along the edge.
steps.text_zh: 先洗手，張大嘴笑，一次看一邊。剛長出來的恆牙門牙比較大，邊緣常常有小小的鋸齒。

steps.en: Tap the chart
steps.zh: 點牙齒圖
steps.text_en: Mark each spot as a baby tooth, an adult tooth, or a gap. Six-year molars are the big teeth right behind your baby molars.
steps.text_zh: 把每個位置標成乳牙、恆牙或空位。六歲臼齒就是乳臼齒後面那顆大大的牙。

steps.en: Find your tooth age
steps.zh: 算出牙齒年齡
steps.text_en: The chart compares your mouth with typical ages and shows that age in 3D. Every child is different, so being a year or two early or late is normal.
steps.text_zh: 牙齒圖會拿你的嘴巴和一般的年齡比較，並在 3D 模型裡顯示那個年齡。每個孩子都不一樣，早一兩年或晚一兩年都很正常。

myths.myth_en: Baby teeth don't matter, because they fall out anyway.
myths.myth_zh: 乳牙反正會掉，蛀了也沒關係。
myths.fact_en: Cavities in baby teeth can hurt and spread. Losing a baby tooth too early can let other teeth drift into the space the adult tooth needs.
myths.fact_zh: 乳牙蛀了一樣會痛，還可能越來越嚴重。乳牙太早掉，旁邊的牙會移過來，占掉恆牙需要的位置。

myths.myth_en: Sugar itself makes holes in your teeth.
myths.myth_zh: 糖本身會在牙齒上蛀出洞。
myths.fact_en: Bacteria eat the sugar and make acid, and the acid makes the holes. How often you snack matters as much as how much sugar you eat.
myths.fact_zh: 是細菌吃了糖產生酸，酸才把牙齒蛀出洞。多常吃零食，和吃了多少糖一樣重要。

myths.myth_en: Brushing harder cleans your teeth better.
myths.myth_zh: 刷牙越用力，牙齒越乾淨。
myths.fact_en: Scrubbing hard can hurt your gums and wear down your teeth. Gentle brushing for two minutes does the job.
myths.fact_zh: 太用力會傷到牙齦、磨損牙齒。輕輕地刷兩分鐘就夠了。

myths.myth_en: Teeth are bones.
myths.myth_zh: 牙齒是骨頭。
myths.fact_en: Teeth and bones are both hard and full of calcium, but teeth are not bones. A bone can heal itself; enamel cannot. That is why teeth are not counted in your 206 bones.
myths.fact_zh: 牙齒和骨頭都很硬、都有很多鈣，但牙齒不是骨頭：骨頭會自己癒合，琺瑯質不會。所以 206 塊骨頭裡沒有算牙齒。

tricks.body_en: Big new molars arrive at the back at about age 6 and again at about age 12.
tricks.body_zh: 大約 6 歲和 12 歲時，後面各長出一組新的大臼齒。

tricks.body_en: Incisors cut, canines grip, and molars grind.
tricks.body_zh: 門牙切、犬齒勾、臼齒磨。

tricks.body_en: Brush two times a day, for two minutes each time, and see the dentist two times a year.
tricks.body_zh: 一天刷兩次、每次刷兩分鐘、一年看兩次牙醫。

tricks.body_en: No sugar for the bacteria means no acid for your teeth.
tricks.body_zh: 不給細菌吃糖，牙齒就不會泡在酸裡。

materials.en: Three hard-boiled eggs and three clear cups
materials.zh: 三顆白煮蛋和三個透明杯子

materials.en: Water, white vinegar, and cola
materials.zh: 清水、白醋和可樂

steps.en: Put one egg in each cup. Cover one with water, one with vinegar, and one with cola.
steps.zh: 每個杯子放一顆蛋，分別倒入清水、白醋和可樂，淹過雞蛋。

steps.en: Watch the vinegar cup for a few minutes. What do you see on the shell?
steps.zh: 觀察白醋杯幾分鐘，蛋殼上出現了什麼？

steps.en: Leave the cups overnight, then take the eggs out and gently feel and look at each shell.
steps.zh: 放置一個晚上，再把蛋拿出來，輕輕摸摸看、仔細看看每個蛋殼。

steps.en: Try brushing the cola egg with a toothbrush and toothpaste. What comes off, and what does not?
steps.zh: 用牙刷和牙膏刷刷看可樂杯的蛋，什麼刷得掉、什麼刷不掉？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: eggshell is not enamel, but both are hard minerals made with calcium, and acid dissolves them. The bubbles in the vinegar show the shell breaking down. The cola egg shows both stains and acid. Remind students that teeth have saliva and fluoride to help them, but they still need brushing and fewer sugary drinks.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：蛋殼不是琺瑯質，但兩者都是含鈣的堅硬礦物，都會被酸溶解。白醋裡冒出的泡泡，就是蛋殼正在分解；可樂杯同時看得到染色和酸的作用。提醒學生：牙齒有口水和氟幫忙，但還是需要刷牙、少喝含糖飲料。

materials.en: Sticky notes or a tally chart on the board
materials.zh: 便利貼，或黑板上的劃記表

materials.en: The 3D model and the tooth chart on this page
materials.zh: 本頁的 3D 模型和牙齒圖

steps.en: Each student counts how many baby teeth they have lost so far.
steps.zh: 每位同學數一數自己到目前為止掉了幾顆乳牙。

steps.en: Make a bar graph: number of lost teeth across the bottom, number of students up the side.
steps.zh: 畫長條圖：橫軸是掉了幾顆牙，縱軸是有幾位同學。

steps.en: Set the 3D model to your class's age. How many baby teeth has it lost?
steps.zh: 把 3D 模型調到你們班的年齡，模型掉了幾顆乳牙？

steps.en: Is everyone the same? What is the most common number?
steps.zh: 每個人都一樣嗎？最常見的是幾顆？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the graph usually spreads out widely, which is a good way to show that a typical age is only an average. Be kind to students who have lost many teeth or none at all: both are normal.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：統計圖通常分布得很開，正好說明「一般的年齡」只是平均值。掉了很多顆或一顆都沒掉的同學都很正常，請溫和地對待。

culture.title_en: Up on the Roof, Down Under the Bed
culture.title_zh: 上牙丟床底，下牙丟屋頂
culture.body_en: In Taiwan, many families have a custom for a lost baby tooth: a lower tooth is thrown up onto the roof, and an upper tooth goes under the bed, so the new tooth will grow in the right direction, toward where the old one went. In many English-speaking countries, children put the tooth under their pillow, and the Tooth Fairy swaps it for a coin. And in Chinese, a wisdom tooth is 智齒 (zhìchǐ), just like in English: it comes in when you are old enough to be wise.
culture.body_zh: 在台灣，很多家庭對掉下來的乳牙有個習俗：下排的牙丟到屋頂上，上排的牙丟到床底下，希望新牙朝著舊牙去的方向，長得又快又直。在許多說英語的國家，孩子會把牙齒放在枕頭下，牙仙子（Tooth Fairy）會把它換成一枚硬幣。還有，中文的「智齒」和英文的 wisdom tooth 意思一樣：等你長到夠有智慧的年紀，它才會長出來。

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If a tooth hurts, your gums bleed or swell, or a tooth gets knocked out, tell an adult right away. A knocked-out adult tooth can sometimes be saved if you see a dentist quickly.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果牙齒痛、牙齦流血或腫起來，或牙齒被撞掉，請馬上告訴大人。被撞掉的恆牙如果很快去看牙醫，有時還救得回來。

lessons.title: How Does Your Body Fight Germs?
lessons.blurb_en: Your body has three walls against germs, and it remembers every enemy it has beaten. Watch white blood cells chase bacteria through a tiny cut, and see why the second fight is so much faster.
lessons.blurb_zh: 身體有三道防線，而且記得每個打敗過的敵人。看白血球在一個小傷口裡追著細菌跑，再看看為什麼第二次交手快得多。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your body fights germs with three walls: skin and mucus keep most germs out, white blood cells attack the ones that get in, and your body remembers each germ so it can win faster next time. That memory is how vaccines work.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 身體用三道防線對抗病菌：皮膚和黏液擋住大部分，白血球攻擊闖進來的，身體還會記住每一種病菌，下次贏得更快——疫苗就是靠這份記憶。

lab.how_en: A paper cut on your fingertip, blown up 2,000 times. Slide the time forward: bacteria slip in and double, the area turns red and swollen, white blood cells squeeze out of a blood vessel to eat them, and Y-shaped antibodies finally tag every last one. Then switch to the second time the same germ shows up, and compare the two fights on the chart.
