paras: Germs are tiny living things, such as bacteria and viruses, that are too small to see. Most bacteria are harmless, and many, like the ones in your gut, even help you. But some can make you sick. Your body is attacked by germs every day, and it wins almost every time, usually without you noticing. It does this with three walls of defense.

The first wall keeps germs out. Your skin is a tough, dry barrier that most germs cannot get through. Your nose, mouth, and throat are lined with sticky mucus that traps germs, and tiny hairs sweep the mucus away so you can swallow or sneeze it out. Tears and saliva contain substances that kill bacteria, and your stomach is filled with strong acid. Germs get in mainly through cuts, or through your eyes, nose, and mouth, often from your own hands.

If germs get past the first wall, the second wall attacks right away. Bacteria can double every 20 minutes, so speed matters. Damaged cells send out alarm signals, and blood vessels nearby widen and leak fluid. That is why a cut turns red, warm, swollen, and sore. Then white blood cells squeeze out of the blood vessels and hunt the germs, swallowing them whole. A single drop of blood carries hundreds of thousands of white blood cells. A fever can help too, because many germs grow more slowly when your body is warmer.

The third wall is the smartest. Special white blood cells study the invader and make antibodies, Y-shaped proteins that fit only that one germ, like a key fits a lock. Antibodies stick to the germs, making them easier to catch and destroy. The first time your body meets a new germ, making the right antibodies can take a week or more, so you may feel sick for days.

But your body remembers. After the fight, memory cells stay on guard for years. If the same germ comes back, they make antibodies in a day or two, and the germ is often gone before you feel sick at all. Vaccines use this memory. A vaccine shows your body a harmless piece or a weakened form of a germ, so your body learns to recognize it without having to get sick first.

You can help your three walls. Wash your hands with soap for at least 20 seconds, especially before eating and after using the toilet. Cover coughs and sneezes with your elbow. Clean cuts and keep them covered. Sleep well and eat well, because a tired body fights germs less well. And remember that antibiotics kill bacteria but do nothing against viruses like colds and flu. Now try the germ calculator and the handwashing timer below the model.
paras_zh: 病菌是像細菌和病毒這樣的小生物，小到眼睛看不見。大部分細菌是無害的，很多甚至對你有幫助，例如腸道裡的細菌；但有些會讓你生病。你的身體每天都受到病菌攻擊，而且幾乎每次都贏，通常你根本沒發現。它靠的是三道防線。
第一道防線把病菌擋在外面。皮膚是一道堅韌、乾燥的屏障，大部分病菌穿不過去。鼻子、嘴巴和喉嚨裡有黏黏的黏液，能黏住病菌，細細的纖毛再把黏液掃走，讓你吞下去或打噴嚏噴出來。眼淚和口水裡有能殺死細菌的物質，胃裡則裝滿了強酸。病菌主要是從傷口，或從眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴進來，常常就是被自己的手帶進來的。
病菌如果闖過第一道防線，第二道防線馬上出動。細菌每 20 分鐘就能多一倍，所以速度很重要。受傷的細胞發出警報，附近的血管變寬、滲出液體，所以傷口會紅、熱、腫、痛。接著白血球從血管裡擠出來追捕病菌，把它們整個吞下去。一滴血裡就有幾十萬個白血球。發燒也能幫忙，因為很多病菌在體溫比較高時長得比較慢。
第三道防線最聰明。特別的白血球會研究入侵者，製造抗體：一種 Y 字形的蛋白質，只配得上那一種病菌，就像一把鑰匙只開一把鎖。抗體黏在病菌上，讓它們更容易被抓住、被消滅。身體第一次遇到新的病菌時，做出對的抗體可能要一個星期以上，所以你可能會不舒服好幾天。
但是身體會記得。打完這一仗，記憶細胞會守候好幾年。同一種病菌再來的時候，它們一兩天就能做出抗體，病菌常常在你感覺不舒服之前就被消滅了。疫苗就是利用這份記憶：疫苗讓身體看到病菌無害的一小部分，或是減弱過的病菌，讓身體不必先生病，就學會認出它。
你也可以幫助這三道防線。用肥皂洗手至少 20 秒，尤其是吃東西前和上完廁所後。咳嗽、打噴嚏時用手肘遮住。傷口要清潔，並且蓋好。睡飽、吃好，因為疲累的身體比較打不贏病菌。還要記得：抗生素能殺細菌，但對感冒、流感這些病毒完全沒用。現在試試模型下方的病菌計算機和洗手計時器。
questions: What are the three walls your body uses against germs?
Why does a cut turn red, warm, and swollen?
Why do you often not get sick the second time the same germ comes back?
answers: First, skin and mucus keep germs out. Second, white blood cells attack germs that get in. Third, antibodies target each germ, and the body remembers it.
Damaged cells send alarm signals, and nearby blood vessels widen and leak fluid so that white blood cells can get to the germs.
Memory cells remember the germ and make antibodies in a day or two, so the germ is gone before you feel sick.

kinds_head.eyebrow: Three Walls of Defense · 三道防線

kinds.text_en: A tough, dry wall. Most germs get in only through cuts, so clean and cover them.
kinds.text_zh: 堅韌又乾燥的牆；大部分病菌只能從傷口進來，所以傷口要清潔、蓋好。

kinds.text_en: Sticky mucus traps germs, tears and saliva fight bacteria, and stomach acid destroys most germs you swallow.
kinds.text_zh: 黏液黏住病菌，眼淚和口水對抗細菌，胃酸消滅大部分吞下去的病菌。

kinds.text_en: Red, warm, swollen, and sore: blood vessels open up so white blood cells can rush in.
kinds.text_zh: 紅、熱、腫、痛：血管打開，讓白血球趕過來。

kinds.where_en: In the blood, ready to leave it
kinds.where_zh: 在血液裡，隨時可以出動
kinds.text_en: Hundreds of thousands in each drop of blood. They squeeze out of blood vessels and swallow germs whole.
kinds.text_zh: 每一滴血裡有幾十萬個；它們從血管擠出來，把病菌整個吞下去。

kinds.where_en: Made by special white blood cells
kinds.text_en: Each antibody fits one germ like a key in a lock. Memory cells remember it for years.
kinds.text_zh: 每一種抗體只配一種病菌，像鑰匙配鎖；記憶細胞能記住它好幾年。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a castle: the walls and the moat keep enemies out, the guards attack anyone who climbs in, and the castle keeps a wanted poster for every enemy it has ever caught.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把身體想成一座城堡：城牆和護城河把敵人擋在外面，衛兵攻擊爬進來的人，城堡還為每個抓過的敵人貼了一張通緝令。

measure.lead_en: Use the calculator below the model to see how fast one bacterium can multiply, then wash your hands with the timer the way Taiwan's CDC teaches: wet, scrub, rinse, scoop, and dry.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的計算機，看一隻細菌能多快變多；再跟著計時器，照疾管署教的「濕、搓、沖、捧、擦」洗手。

steps.en: Do the germ math
steps.zh: 算一算病菌
steps.text_en: Start with one bacterium that doubles every 20 minutes. Slide the hours and watch the number grow. How long until there are more than the 23 million people in Taiwan?
steps.text_zh: 從一隻每 20 分鐘多一倍的細菌開始。拉動時間看數字變大：要多久才會比台灣的 2,300 萬人還多？

steps.en: Wash with the timer
steps.zh: 跟著計時器洗手

steps.text_zh: 到洗手台按下開始，跟著五個步驟做。搓滿 20 秒：手心、手背、指縫、指尖、大拇指和手腕。

steps.en: Check with glitter
steps.zh: 用亮粉檢查
steps.text_en: In class, put a little glitter or flour on your hands, then wash. Any sparkles left show the spots you usually miss.
steps.text_zh: 在課堂上，手上沾一點亮粉或麵粉再洗；還留著亮亮的地方，就是你平常洗不到的地方。

myths.myth_en: All bacteria are bad for you.
myths.myth_zh: 細菌都是壞的。
myths.fact_en: Most bacteria are harmless, and trillions of helpful bacteria live in your gut, where they help digest food and crowd out harmful germs.
myths.fact_zh: 大部分細菌是無害的；腸道裡住著好幾兆個有益的細菌，幫忙消化食物，還把有害的病菌擠走。

myths.myth_en: Antibiotics cure colds.
myths.myth_zh: 抗生素能治感冒。
myths.fact_en: Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics work only on bacteria. Taking them when they are not needed helps bacteria learn to resist them.
myths.fact_zh: 感冒是病毒引起的，抗生素只對細菌有效。不需要時吃抗生素，反而讓細菌學會抵抗它。

myths.myth_en: A fever is always bad and should be stopped.
myths.myth_zh: 發燒一定是壞事，要馬上退燒。
myths.fact_en: A fever is often part of how your body fights germs. A doctor or a parent decides when medicine is needed, especially if the fever is very high or lasts a long time.
myths.fact_zh: 發燒常常是身體對抗病菌的一部分。要不要吃藥由醫生或家長決定，尤其是燒得很高或燒很久的時候。

myths.myth_en: If you can't see dirt, your hands are clean.
myths.myth_zh: 手看起來不髒，就是乾淨的。
myths.fact_en: Germs are far too small to see. Clean-looking hands can still carry them, so wash before you eat and after using the toilet.
myths.fact_zh: 病菌小到看不見，看起來乾淨的手也可能帶著病菌；吃東西前、上完廁所後都要洗手。

tricks.body_en: Skin and mucus keep germs out, white blood cells eat them, and antibodies help your body remember them.
tricks.body_zh: 皮膚和黏液把病菌擋住，白血球把它們吃掉，抗體幫身體記住它們。

tricks.body_en: The four signs of inflammation mean your body is already fighting.
tricks.body_zh: 發炎的四個徵兆，表示身體已經開始作戰。

tricks.body_en: Wet, scrub for 20 seconds, rinse, scoop water to clean the tap, and dry: Taiwan's five steps for washing hands.
tricks.body_zh: 淋濕、搓 20 秒、沖乾淨、捧水洗水龍頭、擦乾：台灣的洗手五步驟。

tricks.body_en: Bacteria yes, viruses no. Colds and flu are viruses.
tricks.body_zh: 細菌有效，病毒沒用；感冒和流感都是病毒。

materials.en: A shallow plate of water and some ground black pepper
materials.zh: 一個裝水的淺盤和一些黑胡椒粉

materials.en: Liquid soap or dish soap
materials.zh: 洗手乳或洗碗精

steps.en: Sprinkle pepper all over the water. The pepper is the “germs.”
steps.zh: 把胡椒粉撒滿整個水面，胡椒粉就是「病菌」。

steps.en: Dip a clean finger into the middle. What happens?
steps.zh: 用乾淨的手指點一下中間，發生了什麼事？

steps.en: Now put a drop of soap on your fingertip and dip it in again.
steps.zh: 在指尖沾一滴肥皂，再點一次。

steps.en: Where did the pepper go? Why?
steps.zh: 胡椒粉跑到哪裡去了？為什麼？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: soap breaks the surface tension of the water, so the pepper rushes away. In real handwashing, soap also breaks up oils on your skin and lifts germs off so the water can rinse them away. That is why rinsing with water alone is not enough.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：肥皂破壞了水的表面張力，所以胡椒粉一下子散開。真正洗手時，肥皂也會分解皮膚上的油脂，把病菌拉起來，讓水把它們沖走——所以只用清水沖是不夠的。

materials.en: A little glitter, flour, or washable paint
materials.zh: 一點亮粉、麵粉或可洗的顏料

materials.en: Soap, water, and paper towels
materials.zh: 肥皂、水和擦手紙

steps.en: One student puts a little glitter on one hand. That is the “germ.”
steps.zh: 一位同學在一隻手上沾一點亮粉，那就是「病菌」。

steps.en: Shake hands down a line of five or six students.
steps.zh: 沿著一排五、六位同學依序握手。

steps.en: Check everyone's hands, then their desks, pencils, and faces. Where did the glitter end up?
steps.zh: 檢查每個人的手，再看看桌子、鉛筆和臉：亮粉跑到哪裡去了？

steps.en: Everyone washes with soap. Who got it all off?
steps.zh: 大家用肥皂洗手，誰洗得最乾淨？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: germs travel the same way, and the last student in line still gets some. Ask how many students touched their face without noticing. Washable materials only, and keep glitter away from eyes.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：病菌就是這樣傳出去的，排到最後的同學一樣會沾到。問問大家有幾個人不知不覺摸了臉。請只用可以洗掉的材料，亮粉不要碰到眼睛。

culture.body_en: The Chinese word for immunity, 免疫 (miǎnyì), means “escaping the plague”: 免 is to avoid, and 疫 is an epidemic. English immunity comes from the Latin immunis, “free from a duty,” so an immune person was free from the sickness. The old saying 病從口入 (bìng cóng kǒu rù), “sickness comes in through the mouth,” is why Taiwanese students learn to wash their hands before every meal, and why the five steps 濕、搓、沖、捧、擦 are posted next to so many sinks.
culture.body_zh: 中文的「免疫」，意思是「免除疫病」：免是避開，疫是流行病。英文 immunity 來自拉丁文 immunis，「免除義務」，所以 immune 的人就是不必生那場病的人。老話說「病從口入」，所以台灣的學生從小就學會飯前洗手，很多洗手台旁邊也貼著「濕、搓、沖、捧、擦」五個字。

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If a cut gets more red, hot, swollen, or painful, or if you have a high fever or feel very sick, tell an adult. Take medicine only when a doctor or a parent says so, and follow the vaccine advice of your doctor and school.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果傷口越來越紅、熱、腫、痛，或發高燒、覺得非常不舒服，請告訴大人。只在醫生或家長說可以的時候吃藥，打疫苗請依照醫生和學校的建議。

lessons.title: Where Does the Water You Drink Go?
lessons.blurb_en: Your two kidneys clean all of your blood about 30 times a day. Follow the water through real 3D kidneys, zoom into one tiny filter, and check whether you are drinking enough today.
lessons.blurb_zh: 兩顆腎臟每天把全身的血洗大約 30 遍。跟著水走過真實的 3D 腎臟，放大看一個小小的過濾器，再看看你今天水喝得夠不夠。
lessons.big_idea_en: Your kidneys are filters. They clean your blood again and again, keep the water and salt your body needs, and send the rest to your bladder as urine.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 腎臟是濾水器：一遍又一遍把血過濾乾淨，留下身體需要的水和鹽，把其餘的變成尿液送到膀胱。

lab.how_en: These are real kidneys, in their real place beside your backbone. Blood flows in, clean blood flows out, and drops of urine run down two thin tubes to the bladder. Slide how much water you drank and watch the urine change. Zoom into a nephron to see the three steps: filter, take back, flush. When the bladder is full, send your model to the restroom!
lab.how_zh: 這是真實的腎臟，就在脊柱兩旁真正的位置。血流進去、乾淨的血流出來，一滴滴尿液沿著兩條細管流到膀胱。拉動「喝了多少水」，看尿液怎麼變。放大一顆腎元，看三個步驟：過濾、回收、排出。膀胱滿了，就讓模型去上廁所吧！

legend.zh: 紅褐色：真實的腎臟

legend.en: Bright red: blood coming in from the heart
legend.zh: 鮮紅色：從心臟來的血

legend.en: Dark red: cleaned blood going back
legend.zh: 暗紅色：過濾後流回去的血

legend.en: Yellow: urine on its way to the bladder
legend.zh: 黃色：流向膀胱的尿液

legend.zh: 腎元裡的藍點：水

lab.scale_en: The bones, kidneys, ureters, and bladder are real shapes from BodyParts3D, in their real places; the blood vessels and the nephron are our own drawing. A real nephron is far too thin to see, and each kidney has about a million of them. Time is sped up: one second here is 20 minutes. The amounts are for a child of about 30 kilograms; an adult's kidneys filter about 140 liters of blood a day.

paras: Take a sip of water. In a few minutes it will be in your blood, and within an hour or two, some of it will be on its way out again. Your body is about 60 percent water, and it has to keep that amount just right. The organs in charge are your two kidneys. They are shaped like beans, each about the size of your fist, and they sit on either side of your backbone, just under your lowest ribs. The right one sits a little lower, because your liver is above it.

Your kidneys are filters for your blood. As your cells work, they make waste, and the blood carries it away. About a fifth of the blood your heart pumps goes straight to the kidneys. In an adult, they filter about half a cup of blood every minute. That adds up to about 140 liters a day, which means all of your blood gets cleaned about 30 times every day.

The cleaning is done by tiny filters called nephrons, and each kidney has about a million of them. A nephron works in three steps. First, it filters: water, salt, sugar, and waste are pushed out of the blood, while blood cells are too big to get through. Second, it takes back: almost all of the water, and all of the sugar your body needs, return to the blood. Third, it flushes: the waste and the extra water that are left become urine.

From 140 liters of filtered blood, only 1 to 2 liters become urine. Urine drips down two thin tubes called ureters into the bladder, a stretchy bag that slowly fills like a balloon. When it is about half full, nerves tell your brain that it is time to find a restroom. Urine is yellow because of a pigment left over when old red blood cells are broken down.

Your kidneys also decide how much water to keep. If you drink a lot, they let more water go, and your urine is pale. If you have not had enough, they hold water back, and your urine turns dark yellow. So the color is a message from your kidneys: pale yellow means you are doing fine, and dark yellow means it is time to drink. You lose water in your sweat and your breath too, so you need more on hot days and when you exercise.

Kidneys work quietly, and people often do not notice a problem until it is serious. Taiwan has one of the highest rates of kidney failure in the world, often after years of diabetes or high blood pressure. You can look after your kidneys now. Drink water instead of sugary drinks: Taiwan's health agency says elementary students need at least 1,500 milliliters a day. Do not eat too much salt, and go to the restroom when you need to. Now count your cups with the water tracker below the model.
paras_zh: 喝一口水。幾分鐘後它就會進到你的血液裡，一兩個小時之內，其中一部分又要準備離開了。你的身體大約 60% 是水，而且必須把水量維持得剛剛好。負責這件事的器官是兩顆腎臟。它們的形狀像豆子，每顆大約和你的拳頭一樣大，位在脊柱兩旁、最下面幾根肋骨的下方。右邊那顆稍微低一點，因為它上面有肝臟。
腎臟是血液的過濾器。細胞工作時會產生廢物，由血液帶走。心臟打出來的血，大約有五分之一直接流向腎臟。大人的腎臟每分鐘大約過濾半杯血，一天加起來大約 140 公升，也就是說，你全身的血每天大約被洗 30 遍。
負責清洗的是很小的過濾器，叫做腎元，每顆腎臟大約有一百萬個。腎元的工作分成三步。第一步，過濾：水、鹽、糖和廢物被擠出血液，血球太大，過不去。第二步，回收：幾乎所有的水，以及身體需要的糖，全部回到血液裡。第三步，排出：剩下的廢物和多餘的水，就成了尿液。
140 公升過濾過的血，只有 1 到 2 公升變成尿液。尿液沿著兩條叫做輸尿管的細管，一滴滴流進膀胱。膀胱是一個有彈性的袋子，像氣球一樣慢慢裝滿。大約半滿的時候，神經會告訴大腦：該去找廁所了。尿液是黃色的，是因為老舊的紅血球被分解後留下了一種色素。
腎臟還會決定要留下多少水。水喝得多，腎臟就多放一些水出去，尿液顏色很淡；水喝得不夠，腎臟就把水留住，尿液變成深黃色。所以尿液的顏色是腎臟給你的訊息：淡黃色表示沒問題，深黃色表示該喝水了。流汗和呼吸也會讓你失去水分，所以天氣熱和運動的時候要喝更多。
腎臟默默工作，等到有感覺時，問題往往已經很嚴重了。台灣是全世界腎臟衰竭比率最高的地方之一，常常是多年的糖尿病或高血壓造成的。你現在就可以照顧自己的腎臟：喝白開水，不要喝含糖飲料——國民健康署說，國小學生每天至少要喝 1,500 毫升的水。不要吃太鹹，想上廁所就去上。現在用模型下方的喝水紀錄，數數你今天喝了幾杯。
questions: What are the three steps a nephron uses to clean the blood?
Why is only a small part of the filtered liquid turned into urine?
What does the color of your urine tell you?
answers: It filters water, salt, sugar, and waste out of the blood; it takes back the water and sugar the body needs; and it flushes the waste and extra water out as urine.
Because the nephrons take almost all of the water, and the things the body needs, back into the blood.
Pale yellow means you have had enough water. Dark yellow means your kidneys are holding water back, and you need to drink.

kinds_head.eyebrow: Your Water System · 身體的排水系統

kinds.where_en: Beside your backbone, under the lowest ribs
kinds.where_zh: 脊柱兩旁、最下面的肋骨下方
kinds.text_en: Two bean-shaped filters, each about the size of your fist. You can live a healthy life with just one.
kinds.text_zh: 兩顆豆子形狀的過濾器，每顆大約和拳頭一樣大；只有一顆也能健康地生活。

kinds.where_en: About a million in each kidney
kinds.where_zh: 每顆腎臟大約一百萬個
kinds.text_en: Each one filters a little blood, returns the water and sugar you need, and sends the waste on.
kinds.text_zh: 每個腎元過濾一點點血，把需要的水和糖送回去，把廢物往下送。

kinds.where_en: From the body's main artery and back to its main vein
kinds.where_zh: 從主動脈來，回到大靜脈
kinds.text_en: About a fifth of the blood from every heartbeat goes to the kidneys.
kinds.text_zh: 每一下心跳打出的血，大約有五分之一流向腎臟。

kinds.where_en: One thin tube from each kidney
kinds.text_en: Each tube is about as long as a ruler. Their walls squeeze in waves, so urine goes down even if you are lying flat.
kinds.text_zh: 每條大約一把尺那麼長；管壁像波浪一樣收縮，所以就算躺著，尿液也會往下流。

kinds.where_en: Low in your belly, inside the hip bones
kinds.text_en: A stretchy bag of muscle. It tells your brain when it is about half full.
kinds.text_zh: 一個有彈性的肌肉袋子；大約半滿時，它會通知大腦。

lessons.kinds_note_en: Think of a water treatment plant: pipes bring dirty water in, a million tiny filters clean it, the clean water goes back to the city, and the waste goes to a holding tank.
lessons.kinds_note_zh: 把它想成一座淨水廠：水管把髒水送進來，一百萬個小濾網把它洗乾淨，乾淨的水送回城市，廢水送到儲水槽。

measure.lead_en: Use the water tracker below the model to count what you drink today, and check the color card the next time you go to the restroom.
measure.lead_zh: 用模型下方的喝水紀錄，數一數你今天喝了多少水；下次上廁所時，對照一下顏色卡。

steps.en: Find your goal
steps.zh: 找出你的目標
steps.text_en: Enter your weight. A common rule is 30 milliliters for each kilogram, and elementary students in Taiwan need at least 1,500 milliliters a day.
steps.text_zh: 輸入你的體重。常用的算法是每公斤 30 毫升；台灣的國小學生每天至少要喝 1,500 毫升。

steps.en: Count your cups
steps.zh: 數一數喝了幾杯
steps.text_en: Tap a cup every time you finish one. Measure your own cup or bottle once so you know how much it holds.
steps.text_zh: 每喝完一杯就點一個杯子。先量一次自己的杯子或水壺裝多少，才知道喝了多少。

steps.en: Check the color
steps.zh: 看看顏色
steps.text_en: Pale yellow is the goal. If it is dark yellow, drink a cup of water now. You need more on hot days and after sports.
steps.text_zh: 淡黃色就是目標。如果是深黃色，現在就喝一杯水。天氣熱和運動之後要喝更多。

myths.myth_en: Everyone needs exactly eight glasses of water a day.
myths.myth_zh: 每個人每天都剛好要喝八杯水。
myths.fact_en: It depends on your size, the weather, and how active you are. A rule many people use is 30 milliliters for each kilogram of body weight.
myths.fact_zh: 要看你的體型、天氣和活動量。很多人用的算法是每公斤體重 30 毫升。

myths.myth_en: The more water you drink, the better.
myths.myth_zh: 水喝得越多越好。
myths.fact_en: Your kidneys can only handle so much at a time, and gulping down a huge amount very fast can make you sick. Small sips through the day work best.
myths.fact_zh: 腎臟一次能處理的量有限，一下子猛灌一大堆水反而會不舒服。一整天小口小口地喝最好。

myths.myth_en: You only need to drink when you feel thirsty.
myths.myth_zh: 口渴的時候再喝就好。
myths.fact_en: By the time you feel thirsty, you are already a little short of water, and children at play often do not notice. Drink at every break.
myths.fact_zh: 覺得口渴時，身體其實已經有點缺水了；小朋友玩得正開心時常常沒發現。每節下課都喝一點吧。

myths.myth_en: You need two kidneys to stay alive.
myths.myth_zh: 要有兩顆腎臟才活得下去。
myths.fact_en: One healthy kidney can do the whole job. That is why a living person can give a kidney to someone whose kidneys have failed.
myths.fact_zh: 一顆健康的腎臟就能完成全部的工作，所以活著的人可以把一顆腎臟捐給腎臟衰竭的人。

tricks.body_en: The three steps of every nephron: push the small stuff out, take back what you need, and flush the rest.
tricks.body_zh: 每個腎元的三個步驟：把小東西擠出去、把需要的拿回來、把剩下的排掉。

tricks.body_en: Pale yellow urine means enough water. Dark yellow means drink up.
tricks.body_zh: 尿液淡黃色表示水喝夠了；深黃色表示快去喝水。

tricks.body_en: Your weight in kilograms times 30 gives a daily water goal in milliliters: 30 kilograms means 900, but schoolchildren need at least 1,500.
tricks.body_zh: 體重（公斤）乘以 30，就是一天喝水的毫升數；30 公斤算出來是 900，但國小學生至少要喝 1,500。

tricks.body_en: Your right kidney is a little lower than your left, because the liver takes up the space above it.
tricks.body_zh: 右邊的腎臟比左邊低一點，因為上面的空間被肝臟占走了。

materials.en: A coffee filter or paper towel, a funnel, and two clear cups
materials.zh: 一張咖啡濾紙或紙巾、一個漏斗和兩個透明杯子

materials.en: Water, a spoonful of sand or rice, and a few drops of food coloring
materials.zh: 水、一匙沙子或米，以及幾滴食用色素

steps.en: Mix the sand and the food coloring into a cup of water. This is your “blood.”
steps.zh: 把沙子和食用色素攪進一杯水裡，這就是你的「血液」。

steps.en: Put the filter in the funnel and pour the mixture through it into the second cup.
steps.zh: 把濾紙放進漏斗，把混合液倒過去，流進第二個杯子。

steps.en: What stayed in the filter? What went through?
steps.zh: 什麼東西留在濾紙上？什麼東西通過了？

steps.en: The color went through with the water. How could you get the water back without the color?
steps.zh: 顏色跟著水一起通過了。要怎麼把水拿回來，卻不要顏色呢？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: the paper filter is like the first step of a nephron: big things, like blood cells, stay behind, and small things go through. But a kidney is much smarter than paper. In the second step, it takes back the water and sugar it wants and leaves the waste, something no simple filter can do.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：濾紙就像腎元的第一步：大的東西（例如血球）留下來，小的東西通過。但腎臟比濾紙聰明得多：第二步，它把想要的水和糖拿回來、把廢物留下，這是簡單的濾紙做不到的。

materials.en: A measuring cup and everyone's own bottle or cup
materials.zh: 一個量杯，和每個人自己的水壺或杯子

materials.en: A tally chart on the board
materials.zh: 黑板上的劃記表

steps.en: Measure how many milliliters each bottle or cup holds.
steps.zh: 量一量每個水壺或杯子可以裝幾毫升。

steps.en: For one school day, make a tally mark every time you finish a bottle or cup.
steps.zh: 上學的一整天，每喝完一壺或一杯就畫一筆。

steps.en: At the end of the day, work out how many milliliters you drank.
steps.zh: 放學前算一算，你總共喝了幾毫升。

steps.en: Who reached 1,500? What could help the class drink more tomorrow?
steps.zh: 誰喝到 1,500 毫升了？明天可以怎麼做，讓全班喝更多水？

activities.tip_en: Teaching tip: this is good practice with multiplication and units. Most students are surprised by how little they drink at school. Agree on a class habit, such as a sip at every bell, and let students go to the restroom when they ask.
activities.tip_zh: 教學提示：這是練習乘法和單位換算的好機會。大多數學生會很驚訝自己在學校喝得這麼少。全班可以約定一個習慣，例如每次鐘響喝一口；學生想上廁所時，也請讓他們去。

culture.body_en: In everyday Chinese and Taiwanese, a kidney is often called 腰子 (yāozi), “the waist one,” because the kidneys sit at the waist. That is also why a cashew is a 腰果 (yāoguǒ), “waist nut”: it is curved just like a kidney. English noticed the same shape in a different food: the kidney bean. And when a Taiwanese family asks 你今天喝水了沒？, “Have you had water today?”, they are looking after two small organs most people never think about.
culture.body_zh: 日常的中文和台語常把腎臟叫做「腰子」，因為腎臟就在腰的位置。腰果也是這樣得名的：它彎彎的形狀就像一顆腰子。英文在另一種食物上看到同樣的形狀：kidney bean，中文正好也叫「紅腰豆」。家人問你「今天喝水了沒？」的時候，其實是在照顧兩顆大多數人從來沒想過的小器官。

lessons.health_en: This lesson is for learning about the body. It is not medical advice. If it hurts when you go to the restroom, if your urine looks red or brown, or if you are very thirsty all the time, tell an adult. Take medicine only when a doctor or a parent says so, because some medicines are hard on the kidneys.
lessons.health_zh: 本課是認識身體的教材，不是醫療建議。如果上廁所時會痛、尿液看起來是紅色或褐色，或是一直覺得非常口渴，請告訴大人。只在醫生或家長說可以的時候吃藥，因為有些藥會傷腎。
